clean_body: Callais and Its Consequences - By Justin Riemer, President, USGI, and Marshal Trigg, Junior Counsel, USGI - On April 29, the Supreme Court handed... | | | | | | | | | Callaisand Its Consequences By Marshal Trigg, Counsel, USGI On April 29, the Supreme Court handed down its 6 to 3 decision in , holding that the state’s 250-mile, snake-shaped 6th Congressional District—linking the populations of Shreveport, Alexandria, Lafayette, and Baton Rouge to create a second majority-minority district—amounted to an unconstitutional racial gerrymander. The ripple effects have been fast and wide-ranging, as are the longer-term implications for future redistricting fights.The day after the ruling, Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry , and was subsequently hit with which are currently pending. On May 4, the Court the Callais plaintiffs’ request to expedite issuance of the judgment, waiving the usual 32-day waiting period and enabling the state legislature to enact a remedial map. The same day, Florida its own redistricting legislation. Tennessee on May 7. On May 11, the Court blocking Alabama from using its legislature-drawn map, and relisted for conference two pending cases on whether private litigants may sue under Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act. South Carolina’s House a procedural step on May 6 toward a possible redraw, but then in the Senate. The situation there . has called off any moves until 2027, and will convene a June 17 special session to draw maps for the 2028 cycle. Democratic-led states are coordinated responses on the same timeline, . All of this on top of the Virginia Supreme Court’s ruling invalidating the state’s gerrymandering referendum make for a dizzying array of redistricting activity as we enter primary season. Callais is likely to reshape redistricting fights well into the next decade. By raising the evidentiary bar for Section 2 vote-dilution claims and drawing a sharper line between race and partisanship in map-drawing, the decision cuts into the leverage Section 2 plaintiffs have exercised under the Gingles framework that has structured these claims since 1986. Expect states under court-ordered remedial maps to push to modify or dissolve those orders. The Court’s order in Alabama this week is the first real signal. The has indicated it will revisit districts where race predominated in line-drawing under the old Section 2 framework. And by reducing Section 2 litigation risk for legislatures, the ruling reinforces the mid-decade trend already well underway. Although congressional redistricting will get much of the attention, the ramifications extend to state legislative and local redistricting and question the viability of state-level “Voting Rights Acts” that incorporate race-based criteria, one of which has already been . The Supreme Court’s ruling arrived in the middle of an already unprecedented, combustible mid-decade redistricting cycle and poured fuel on it. The 2026 midterms will offer a first read on the consequences; 2028 and 2030 will tell the longer story. | | | | | | | Ballotpedia Spring Report Ballotpedia "" its State of Election Policy Legislation 2026 Spring Report, which finds that state legislatures enacted 236 election-related bills across 34 states in the first four months of 2026. The report highlights various specific policy areas including proof-of-citizenship laws, ranked-choice voting legislation, and mid-decade redistricting activity.Arizona Pima County is to ensure open lines of communication between all the offices that play a role in elections.District of Columbia Voters in the June 16 primary and D.C. Council special election under Initiative 83, approved by voters in 2024. Voters will be able to rank up to five candidates in each race.Georgia The State Board of Elections to decide the state’s new method of voting. This decision came after the legislature voted to ban the current system that utilizes a QR code for ballot tabulation. The SBOE stated that this is a decision for the legislature, who adjourned for the year without creating a new system to replace the QR code system.Indiana The Henry County Election Board that a programming error in electronic ballots during the Republican primary allowed some voters residing in Wayne Township Precincts 1, 2, and 3 but outside the town limits of Knightstown to cast ballots in the town’s clerk-treasurer and town council races. Officials said there is no way to determine how many ineligible votes were cast; the unofficial results show the clerk-treasurer race separated by three votes. Unofficial results showed the Town Treasurer primary contest was separated by three votes. Iowa Secretary of State Pate has complied with the U.S. Department of Justice’s request for the state’s complete voter file. Louisiana that invalidated the state’s congressional district maps, Governor Landry until July so the Legislature can redraw the maps. Maryland State Senate President Bill Ferguson, who last year opposed a push to redraw the state’s congressional map, he is now open to discussing a path forward. The emerging effort would aim to eliminate the Eastern Shore district of Representative Andy Harris, the state’s lone Republican and chair of the House Freedom Caucus.Michigan A Wayne County clerk to the DOJ’s demand for 2024 election ballots, receipts, and envelopes from the county by informing Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon in writing that the county is not the legal custodian of those records, which under Michigan law are maintained by municipal clerks. A state court all felony charges against former Adams Township Clerk Stephanie Scott and attorney Stefanie Lambert Junttila, who had been accused of permitting an unauthorized analyst to access electronic poll book data from the 2020 general election. The court held that although the voter data at issue is exempt from disclosure under Michigan’s Freedom of Information Act, the statute imposes no separate confidentiality or nondisclosure requirement, and that creating such a requirement would exceed what the legislature enacted. A misdemeanor charge against Scott for disobeying instructions from the Secretary of State remains pending.Mississippi Governor Reeves the special legislative session scheduled for May 20 to redraw the state’s Supreme Court districts, after the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit vacated the federal district court order that required the state to redraw its map. Reeves indicated that congressional redistricting will likely be deferred to the 2027 regular legislative session absent a further special session.Missouri Boone County Clerk Brianna Lennon Secretary of State Hoskins in writing that she will not revise voter rolls to reflect the state’s new congressional map until Hoskins issues a determination on whether the People Not Politicians referendum petition has gathered sufficient signatures to qualify for the ballot.Nevada Ahead of the June 9 primary, the Washoe County Registrar of Voters new signature-verification software that will, for the first time, analyze the signatures on mail ballot envelopes and route matching ballots directly to precinct sorting without human review. Officials project this will improve mail-ballot processing efficiency by 15 to 20%. Ballots whose signatures the software cannot match will be referred to a bipartisan team for manual review; if the signature remains unverified, the ballot is challenged.New Jersey Henrilynn Ibezim, a former Democratic mayoral candidate in Plainfield, to forging hundreds of voter registration applications. Federal prosecutors Prosecutors say the defendants also falsely stated on their naturalization paperwork that they had never voted or registered to vote in a federal election. The New Jersey GOP the formation of an Election Integrity Task Force, comprised of state party officials and several county election commissioners and administrators, to identify and address irregularities in New Jersey’s election system and to complement the Republican National Committee’s ongoing efforts in the state. New Mexico plagued the first day of early voting in the June 2 primary election, affecting the state’s same-day voter registration system in a handful of counties. Officials said the disruptions were resolved within hours and impacted voters were still able to cast provisional ballots.New York Congresswoman Claudia Tenney to Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche regarding New York legislation that would automatically register Medicaid applicants and enrollees. Rep. Tenney cites to verification problems and the large numbers of noncitizen enrollees as grounds for the Department of Justice to evaluate whether the legislation would violate the National Voter Registration ActOhio Advocacy groups are of the grace period for the delivery of mail ballots to local Board of Elections. This comes after the Legislature passed a bill eliminating the grace period, requiring all absentee ballots be returned by 7:30 PM on Election Day.The United States Department of Homeland Security into potential voting fraud in Franklin County. Over 50 individuals are named in this investigation. The investigation appears to be focused on non-citizen voting. Pennsylvania Lehigh County officials that the county election office had inadvertently used the May 2025 voter rolls to mail out ballots for the May 19, 2026 primary, resulting in hundreds of erroneous mail-in ballots being sent to voters who had since moved, changed parties, or died, and to some voters who had not requested mail ballots in the 2026 cycle. About 115 individuals who changed their party affiliation in the last year received the wrong ballot.South Carolina A push to allow the South Carolina General Assembly to return after the regular session ends to consider mid-decade congressional redistricting in the state Senate after a 29-17 vote fell two votes short of the required two-thirds majority.Tennessee After the General Assembly passed and Governor Lee signed a new congressional map during a special session, county election officials to redraw precinct boundaries and update voter records ahead of the August primary. The changes affect roughly 75% of voters in Davidson County, where officials plan to mail new registration cards to all voters.Utah Lieutenant Governor Henderson that the initiative petition to repeal Proposition 4—the 2018 voter-approved law creating an independent redistricting commission—failed to qualify for the 2026 ballot. Although the effort, backed by Utahns for Representative Government, exceeded the statewide signature threshold, it met the required 8 percent threshold in only 24 of Utah’s 29 state Senate districts, two short of the 26 required.Virginia Governor Spanberger that Virginia has rejoined the Electronic Registration Information Center (ERIC) as its 27th member state, reversing the 2023 withdrawal directed by former Governor Youngkin. Elections Commissioner Steven Koski said the state will integrate ERIC’s cross-state movers, in-state movers, duplicate-registration, and deceased-voter reports into its voter list maintenance procedures.Wisconsin The Wisconsin Elections Commission the City of Madison and Dane County boards of canvassers to un-count 23 absentee ballots from the April 7 election, finding that although the ballots had been received by the city clerk’s office before the Monday before Election Day, a courier delay caused them to arrive at their polling places after the statutory 8 p.m. deadline. In a separate unanimous action, the commission ordered Mequon and Ozaukee County to count five absentee ballots that had been excluded based on disputed witness-address requirements.The FBI a senior Wisconsin elections official about aspects of the 2020 presidential election in the state. The official has not been publicly identified, and investigators have not disclosed whether the interview is connected to a grand jury or other criminal inquiry. | | | Alabama Allen v. Milligan, No. 2:21-cv-1291 (N.D. Ala.) On May 11, the U.S. Supreme Court Alabama’s emergency application to stay the injunctions that had required the state to use a court-imposed congressional map containing two majority-black districts. The ruling came less than two weeks after the Court’s April 29 decision in Louisiana v. Callais , which held that race may not predominate in the drawing of legislative districts.Arizona Pinal County v. Fontes, No. CV2026-003106 (Ariz. Super. Ct., Maricopa Cnty.) On May 1, a state court that Secretary of State Fontes exceeded his authority by adopting a provision of the state Elections Procedures Manual that required precinct-based counties to allow voters who appeared at the wrong polling place to cast a provisional ballot using an accessible voting device programmed with all of the county’s ballot styles. The court found that the requirement would effectively force Pinal County—the only Arizona county still using a precinct-based system—to adopt a vote center model, a decision the court held is reserved by statute to county boards of supervisors. Heap v. Galvin, No. CV2025-020621 (Ariz. Super. Ct., Maricopa Cnty.) The Maricopa County Board of Supervisors a state court to stay its April ruling that had ordered the Board to return information technology systems and certain election-related duties to County Recorder Justin Heap. The Board argued that implementing the ruling immediately would disrupt ongoing local elections in Tempe and Guadalupe and could cost the county tens of millions of dollars to build separate IT systems.District of Columbia DSCC v. Trump, No. 1:26-cv-01114 (D.D.C.) On May 1, the U.S. Department of Justice this consolidated challenge to President Trump’s March 31 executive order on mail voting, arguing the suit is premature because no agency has implemented the order. Supporting declarations from the U.S. Postal Service, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, and the Social Security Administration state that each agency is still deliberating and has not reached final decisions. A coalition of Republican attorneys general led by Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway separately filed a brief defending the order. The court has scheduled a hearing for May 14.Florida Florida Decides Healthcare, Inc. v. Byrd, No. 4:25-cv-00211 (N.D. Fla.) On April 30, a federal court a challenge to state restrictions on citizen-led ballot initiatives. The ruling allows the state to continue enforcing provisions that shorten petition-return deadlines, and require petition circulators to be Florida residents and U.S. citizens and to register with the state. The court found that the legislature was authorized to “protect the integrity” of the initiative process.Thompson-Wynn v. Byrd, No. 2026-ca-000925 (Fla. 2d Jud. Cir., Leon Cnty.) On May 4, two national advocacy organizations and a group of Florida voters in state court. The lawsuit alleges that the new map violates the Fair Districts Amendment, which prohibits partisan gerrymandering. Two similar lawsuits were filed the same day by the and Pitts v. United States, No. 1:26-cv-00809 (N.D. Ga.) On May 6, a federal court Fulton County’s request to force DOJ to return more than 600 boxes of 2020 election ballots and records seized by the FBI earlier this year as part of an investigation into alleged election irregularities. The court held that the county failed to show the government acted with “callous disregard” for constitutional rights.Quinn v. Raffensperger, No. 1:24-cv-04364 (N.D. Ga.) On May 11, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit an effort by two voters to revive a lawsuit seeking to compel Secretary of State Raffensperger to investigate alleged voter roll irregularities. The court held the plaintiffs lacked standing.Illinois Ives v. Pritzker, No. 3:26-cv-03158 (C.D. Ill.) On May 8, the Public Interest Legal Foundation in federal court on behalf of former state legislator Jeanne Ives challenging the Illinois Voting Rights Act of 2011, arguing that the statute mandates the use of race in drawing legislative districts and therefore violates the Fifteenth Amendment and the federal Voting Rights Act under the U.S. Supreme Court’s recent decision in Louisiana v. Callais.Louisiana Louisiana v. Callais, No. 3:24-cv-00122 (W.D. La.) On May 4, the Supreme Court allowing the recent decision to take effect ahead of the normal schedule. The order clears the way for Louisiana to redraw congressional districts before the 2026 midterms.Bernard v. Landry, No. 3:26-cv-00487 (M.D. La.) On May 4, five individual voters, the League of Women Voters of Louisiana, and the League of Women Voters of Louisiana Education Fund in federal court against Secretary of State Landry challenging Governor Landry’s April 30 executive order suspending the state’s May 16 congressional primary, after early voting had already begun, to allow the legislature to redraw the state’s congressional map following the U.S. Supreme Court’s decision in Louisiana v. Callais. Separate lawsuits were filed by a and the v. Landry, No. 3:22-cv-178 (M.D. La.) On May 7, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit striking down Louisiana’s state legislative map, and remanded to the district court for consideration following the U.S. Supreme Court’s ruling in Louisiana v. Callais.Michigan Mantravadi v. Mich. Bureau of Elections, No. 24-000038-MZ (Mich. Ct. Cl.) that the Bureau of Elections cannot withhold records identifying which voters cast their ballots in person on Election Day, by absentee ballot, or during early voting. The Bureau had begun redacting that information after the 2022 adoption of early voting, arguing that combining it with other public data could reveal individual voters’ choices in low-turnout precincts and thereby violate the right to a secret ballot. The court found that this “theoretical” risk was insufficient to justify withholding records that had previously been public, but ordered a further hearing to consider whether a narrower compromise might satisfy both Michigan’s Freedom of Information Act and ballot secrecy concerns.Mississippi White v. State Bd. of Election Comm’rs, No. 4:22-cv-62 (N.D. Miss.) On May 11, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit the federal district court’s 2025 liability order that had required Mississippi to redraw its state Supreme Court districts, and remanded the case for further proceedings in light of Louisiana v. Callais. On May 12, the federal district court the parties to submit a joint status report proposing how the case should proceed.Missouri Healey v. Missouri& Wise v. Missouri, Nos. SC101570 (Mo.) & SC101572 (Mo.); Maggard v. Missouri, No. 2516-CV29597 (Mo.) On May 12, the state Supreme Court upholding the state’s 2025 congressional map and affirming that the map will be used for the 2026 elections. In the from Jackson County, the court ruled that challengers had not shown the map “clearly and undoubtedly” violates the Missouri Constitution’s compactness requirement. In , an appeal from Cole County, the court held that the submission of more than 300,000 referendum signatures by People Not Politicians did not automatically suspend the new map pending a statewide vote, affirming a circuit court ruling in favor of Secretary of State Hoskins.Montana Mont. Fed’n of Pub. Emps. v. Montana, No. XDDV-25-2025-268 (Mont. 1st Jud. Dist. Ct., Lewis & Clark Cnty.)On May 8, a state court enforcement of a law that reduced same-day registration to a five-hour window, while upholding a voter ID law.North Carolina Pierce v. N.C. State Bd. of Elections, No. 4:23-cv-193 (E.D.N.C.) On May 11, plaintiffs of their appeal challenging state Senate Districts 1 and 2 as racial gerrymanders under Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act. The court granted the dismissal the same day, ending federal litigation over the two northeastern districts.Ohio State ex rel. Shannon v. Ogg, Slip Op. No. 2026-Ohio-1599 On May 4, the state Supreme Court that petitioners seeking to recall Whitehall Mayor Michael Bivens and two city councilmembers failed to gather enough valid signatures to place the recall on the ballot. The court found that Whitehall’s clerk of council improperly certified the petitions because the campaigns had not met the city charter’s signature threshold requirements. The ruling halted the planned recall election while organizers attempt to gather additional signatures and continue the effort.Tennessee NAACP Tenn. State Conf. v. Tennessee, No. 26-0591-II **(Davidson Cnty. Ch. Ct.) On May 7, the Tennessee NAACP in state court seeking to block Tennessee’s newly enacted congressional map. The complaint alleges the Republican-led mid-decade redistricting violates Tennessee law and the state constitution, including a longstanding prohibition on changing congressional districts between census cycles that lawmakers repealed during a special legislative session. The state on May 8, stating the suit failed to identify “imminent harm.” Sherman v. Hargett, No. 3:26-cv-00616 (M.D. Tenn.) On May 11, the American Civil Liberties Union and ACLU of Tennessee in federal court challenging the state’s newly enacted congressional map. The complaint alleges that the legislature enacted the map with discriminatory purpose in violation of the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Amendments and in retaliation against voters in the former Ninth Congressional District in violation of the First Amendment, and seeks an order restoring the 2022 map for the 2026 election.Hale v. Lee, No. 3:26-cv-00603 (M.D. Tenn.) On May 12, a federal court on plaintiffs’ request for a temporary restraining order blocking the state’s newly enacted congressional map. This date would fall five days after the May 15 candidate-qualifying deadline established by the same legislation. Plaintiffs—comprising the state party, four Democratic congressional candidates, and four voters—filed a motion he same day seeking an immediate hearing by May 15, arguing that the later date risks voter confusion and would force candidate-plaintiffs to campaign in districts they contend are unlawfully drawn.U.S. Virgin Islands Moorhead v. Fawkes, No. 1:26-cv-00006 (D.V.I.) On May 1, three candidates for territorial office in federal court challenging several Virgin Islands ballot-access rules and a recent settlement between the Democratic Party of the Virgin Islands and election officials. The complaint asks the court to strike down the 200-signature requirement for independent delegate candidates, invalidate a “dual-certification framework” established through the Democratic Party settlement, and bar election officials from rejecting petition signatures from voters classified as inactive. The plaintiffs argue the current system imposes unequal burdens on similarly situated candidates in violation of the First and Fourteenth Amendments and exceeds statutory authority.Virginia Scott v. McDougle, No. CL25-1582-00 (Va. Cir. Ct., Tazwell Cnty.) On May 11, state officials with U.S. Supreme Court Chief Justice John Roberts seeking to stay the Supreme Court of Virginia’s May 8 decision invalidating the voter-approved redistricting amendment and its resulting congressional map. The Virginia court held that the General Assembly violated the state constitution by holding the first of two required votes on the amendment after early voting in the 2025 general election had already begun, on the theory that the constitutional requirement of an “intervening election” between the votes had not been satisfied. The applicants argue that this interpretation rests on a “grave misreading” of federal election law, which they contend defines an “election” as occurring on a single day, and that the Virginia court therefore “transgressed the ordinary bounds of judicial review.”West Virginia United States v. Warner, No. 2:26-CV-00156-TEJ (S.D. W. Va.) On April 29, Secretary of State Warner the DOJ’s lawsuit seeking unredacted voter registration data, arguing that the demand exceeds the agency’s statutory authority under Title III of the Civil Rights Act of 1960 and that state law permits release only of redacted records. The filing further argues that the DOJ’s stated purpose has shifted from list-maintenance review to immigration enforcement, placing the request outside Title III’s scope. Wisconsin On May 5, Dane County in state court challenging a Wisconsin Elections Commission decision rejecting 23 absentee ballots cast in Madison’s April 1 election after city officials delivered the ballots to polling locations after the statutory 8 p.m. deadline. The county argues the commission exceeded its authority and unlawfully disenfranchised voters who timely returned their ballots but were affected by administrative errors outside their control.Honig v. Wisconsin Elections Commission, No. 2026CV001463 (Wis. Cir. Ct., Dane Cnty.)** On May 6, an advocacy group in state court challenging a Wisconsin Elections Commission order directing officials not to count 23 absentee ballots cast in Madison’s April 7 election. The lawsuit argues the ballots were timely completed and submitted by voters, and that rejecting the ballots because election officials delivered them to polling places after 8 p.m. violates the Wisconsin Constitution. | | | | Fox News on the Republican National Committee’s multimillion-dollar election integrity push ahead of the midterms.On May 11, Committee on House Administration Chairman Bryan Steil the Campaign Finance Transparency Act and the Preventing Foreign Interference In American Elections Act. The legislation aims to “increase transparency and ensure fraudulent and foreign donations cannot influence political campaigns, individual candidates, or electoral outcomes.” | | | Hans von Spakovsky and Meaghan McManus that recent voter fraud prosecutions across several states demonstrate the need for Congress to pass the SAVE America Act.A Washington Post editorial that only congressional action limiting redistricting to once per census cycle can halt the growing cycle of retaliatory map-drawing. | | | This study the hypotheses that, from 2012 to 2022, higher quality County Election Administration (CEA) leads to higher public confidence in election results and enhances this confidence among election losers. These hypotheses are evaluated using the new CEA index. Using the Survey of the Performance of American Elections data (from 2012 to 2022), coupled with multi‐level modeling, this study evaluates the impact of CEA on public confidence for election winners and losers. The study ultimately finds that higher quality CEA helps close the confidence gap between election losers and winners.A by Stephen Richer and Adam Ginsburg looks at how courts evaluate Election Day requests to extend polling hours. | | | The Grant Institute has potential openings for junior level attorneys and others interested in the study of election administration and voting issues. Last week I had the chance to speak with students involved in Music City Construction Careers, a program connecting young people to real trades, real skills, and real futures. Electricians, plumbers, pipefitters, HVAC technicians, ironworkers. Careers that build the world around us and pay $60,000 a year or more for those who complete an apprenticeship.

Walking into that room and seeing those students reminded me of something we say too rarely in politics: some of the most essential, most dignified, most in demand work in this country is done by people who learned with their hands.
**Our job as leaders is to make sure every student sees a door open for them, and programs like these are what I am fighting for during my campaign for Congress.[Can I count on you to chip in and help the next generation?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1e60f777-144a-46bd-a28e-ae595440d404?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

That is what Hometowns Over Headlines means to me in practice. It means showing up for the students in Nashville classrooms, not just the donors in Washington conference rooms. It means investing in pathways that lead to real wages, real stability, and real pride in the work you do.
Our nation's next generation deserves leaders who take their future seriously. Leaders who fund the programs that work, protect the educators who show up, and refuse to let political games get in the way of a kid finding their purpose.

Last week I had the chance to speak with students involved in Music City Construction Careers, a program connecting young people to real trades, real skills, and real futures. Electricians, plumbers, pipefitters, HVAC technicians, ironworkers. Careers that build the world around us and pay $60,000 a year or more for those who complete an apprenticeship. | | ---|---|--- Walking into that room and seeing those students reminded me of something we say too rarely in politics: some of the most essential, most dignified, most in demand work in this country is done by people who learned with their hands. # **Endorsements: Here’s Who’s Standing With Our Campaign**
I wanted to take a moment to share some exciting updates from the campaign.**Over the past few months, we’ve built incredible momentum across Texas’s 8th District.** In addition to our win in the Democratic Primary, that momentum is being recognized by leaders and organizations across our community. I’m proud to have earned the support of a broad coalition who believe in our vision for accountable, people-first leadership.**So far, we’ve received endorsements and distinctions from:**
* The Houston Chronicle
* Houston LGBTQ+ Political Caucus
* Secular Houston
* Progressive Voters Network
* Harris County Young Democrats
* Area 5 Democrats

The mask is off. They have canceled elections, introduced a new white majority district, and told a Black Democrat to “shut up, boy.” In response, voters are rallying behind farmer and Democrat for US
| | | | | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001oj8oM5SJP1ZgwfL7lm9v3th1Fo42EaZTymUGJwbUugdTtHWAltUJAim_w4noiZ0HwfvMP5rLLJae1evob7U3L9YX3vYXBGOeRjtiWJXkvsGFsiB5UriASfQvgu1xFOXQc2-ggZiPcK899Crzh8VHDGzkQnf5taiYxUTKJQCuabpbMFmBtbG-gEFblSPVtfNW1MgEMb_OUB5uhFmIsgmJ72TQAQE_MDe_&c=Sh3oIiqVcKI6pRtD8zq2uamJcuF1L4ZMU1YHX4vgx3ej0VyxvOZH-A==&ch=0q-6LK1quxWcluZcqqy4P-l-BQPDiISIyDpV0J8W43uFnUgGvadgkA==)
---
| Peter,
I need to be honest with you: what is happening in Louisiana is not politics as usual- but it is not new.
The Supreme Court weakened the Voting Rights Act, Louisiana republicans suspended the House election, the secretary of state threw out 40k ballots, and as of yesterday, the GOP Republicans have advanced a congressional map to eliminate one of our Black majority districts.
And in the middle of it all, the Republican Senator behind the new map turned to the Executive Director of the Louisiana Democratic Party, a Black man, and said: "Shut up, boy."
History is repeating itself until we make bold moves to change it. And if we don't stand against them now, the cruelty won't stop here.
That is why the Louisiana Democratic Party is proudly standing behind Jamie Davis for United States Senate. He is our man to take a stand against far-right Senator Bill Cassidy and reclaim our US Senate seat.
---
| | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001oj8oM5SJP1ZgwfL7lm9v3th1Fo42EaZTymUGJwbUugdTtHWAltUJAim_w4noiZ0HwfvMP5rLLJae1evob7U3L9YX3vYXBGOeRjtiWJXkvsGFsiB5UriASfQvgu1xFOXQc2-ggZiPcK899Crzh8VHDGzkQnf5taiYxUTKJQCuabpbMFmBtbG-gEFblSPVtfNW1MgEMb_OUB71ixH_UqoOL5HhLXGhXOhS&c=Sh3oIiqVcKI6pRtD8zq2uamJcuF1L4ZMU1YHX4vgx3ej0VyxvOZH-A==&ch=0q-6LK1quxWcluZcqqy4P-l-BQPDiISIyDpV0J8W43uFnUgGvadgkA==)

In response to our election coup, voters are rallying behind farmer and Democrat for US Senate Jamie Davis.
Jamie is a farmer who works the same land his grandfather worked as a sharecropper. He knows the history of where we have come from, and he knows what is at stake in this moment.
When he is elected, he will be the first Black person ever elected to the US Senate from Louisiana.
He knows what it is like to rise up against every conceivable obstacle and build a life for your family, and he is not afraid to speak the clear truth to these Jim Crow tactics.
He knows that this is the moment to declare that we are not going back.
[We know that Jamie is our strongest chance to fight back against this segregationist power grab and mobilize voters across Louisiana. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

subject: No BS
body:
You deserve a Governor who tells it to you straight
[ ](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260514-1.uaoN_2&refcode=em-20260514-1&t=1&akid=1384%2E1086043%2E2CTlhh)
Peter, you deserve a Governor who tells it to you straight -- no BS, no misleading talking points. And these emails? They’re no exception.
**[So today, I’m asking you to split a donation between my reelection campaign and Wes Moore-- and I want to give you three reasons why:](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260514-1.uaoN_2&refcode=em-20260514-1&t=2&akid=1384%2E1086043%2E2CTlhh)**
1. **Nothing is guaranteed in Pennsylvania.** Yes, we’re in the lead right now -- and that’s a testament to the strength of this team. But elections can change on a dime, _especially_ in a battleground state like Pennsylvania. Translation? We need to run this race like we’re 10 points behind.

2. **The far-right attacks have barely even started.** If you think this race is getting nasty now, just wait. That means we need to be prepared for anything that comes our way -- true _or_ untrue.

3. **Mar-a-Lago’s finest are all lined up behind my opponent.** That’s a lot of money -- and a lot of power -- to take on alone. But if this grassroots team continues to step up? That beats any gold-plated Mar-a-Lago fundraiser in my book.

**[We can’t wait until October to get in the game, Peter. The hard work, the preparation, and the training starts right now. Please: Split a donation between our campaign here in Pennsylvania and Wes Moore in Maryland to keep the most competitive states in the country out of Donald Trump’s hands.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260514-1.uaoN_2&refcode=em-20260514-1&t=3&akid=1384%2E1086043%2E2CTlhh)**

History has shown us that there's nothing we can't accomplish if we work together. **No state in America has ever elected a Native American woman as Governor — but with your support, I know we can change that.

# With Gratitude for Your Support

---
|
---
|
---
| |
Dear Friend,

One of my favorite parts of the book of Job is when Job corrects his friends and tells them **real faith requires maintaining faith when things go our way AND when things don’t go our way.** In the wins and in the losses. That’s a hard thing to do, but worth it.
Tuesday’s results were not what we hoped for, but **I am deeply grateful to every supporter, volunteer, friend, and family member who stood with us throughout our campaign.**
We took our message across West Virginia and proved that **hard work, faith, and our grassroots conservative voices still matter.**
I congratulate our Republican nominee, US Senator Shelley Moore Capito, on her victory. She ran a great race that I was not able to overcome. I called her Tuesday evening to convey this same message and congratulate her.
**Now is the time for all of us Republicans to come together and support our Republican nominee, Shelley, for the future of our state and our country.** We must send a Republican to represent West Virginia in DC. The primary voters have spoken, and Shelley is our choice for the US Senate now.
Thank you to all who supported me for believing in our campaign and in the vision we fought for together.**I am full of gratitude and peace that we ran our race well and made lots of new friends along the way.**
God bless you all,
**Tom Willis**

If you've scrolled through Facebook lately, you've probably seen one of two takes on the recent redistricting fight. Either the U.S. Supreme Court "gutted" the Voting Rights Act, or conservatives finally got the green light to redraw any map they want. Both takes are wrong, and the actual story has moved fast over the last two weeks.
I think we owe our neighbors a straight explanation, without the talk-radio heat or the social-media hype. Here is part one of two.
Start with the U.S. Supreme Court. On April 29, the Court decided a case called Louisiana v. Callais. The vote was 6-3. Justice Samuel Alito wrote the majority opinion.
After the 2020 census, Louisiana drew a new congressional map. A federal court said the map likely violated Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, the part of federal law that bans practices that dilute minority voting strength. Louisiana's Legislature then drew a second majority-Black district to fix the problem. A different group of voters sued, saying the new map was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, meaning race had been the main factor in drawing the lines.
The Supreme Court agreed with the second group. It ruled that Louisiana was not actually required to draw a second majority-Black district, so race-based map-drawing was not justified. Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act still exists. Anyone telling you the Voting Rights Act is gone is wrong. But the legal test plaintiffs have to pass in these cases is now significantly harder. Basically, the bar moved.
Now to Mississippi. We have a related case that has been moving through the federal courts. Our three state Supreme Court districts -- Northern, Central, and Southern -- have not been redrawn since 1987. In August 2025, U.S. District Judge Sharion Aycock, a George W. Bush appointee, ruled those districts violate Section 2, especially the Central District that covers the Delta and Jackson area. She ordered them redrawn. The 2026 regular session of the Legislature ended without a new map. Governor Tate Reeves then called a special session for May 20 to comply with the order before the federal court imposed one.
Here is where the story changed. On Monday, May 11, the U.S. Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals vacated Judge Aycock's order and sent the case back to her court for reconsideration under the new Callais standard. The motion to do that was filed jointly by both sides -- the NAACP, ACLU and other plaintiffs on one side, the State of Mississippi on the other. Both agreed the legal ground had shifted under their feet.
What does this mean? The order requiring Mississippi to redraw the Supreme Court districts no longer exists. The case is not closed -- Judge Aycock will look at it again under the tougher Callais standard, and the plaintiffs can amend their arguments. As of this writing, it is not clear whether the Governor will still hold the May 20 special session, postpone it, or use the call for other redistricting matters.
That is the immediate situation. One Supreme Court ruling. One federal-court order, now vacated. One special session, now cancelled. Three weeks ago this looked like a forced march to redraw judicial districts. Today it looks like the system pumping the brakes to apply new precedent.
In part two, I will get into what the Legislature actually has to decide, the louder argument about Mississippi's congressional map, and what all of this might mean for us in Mississippi.

clean_body: The judge gave the Mississippi Legislature the chance to redraw the lines themselves. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? from the desk ofDana Criswell Part One - US Supreme Court Decision | | | May 14 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- If you've scrolled through Facebook lately, you've probably seen one of two takes on the recent redistricting fight. Either the U.S. Supreme Court "gutted" the Voting Rights Act, or conservatives finally got the green light to redraw any map they want. Both takes are wrong, and the actual story has moved fast over the last two weeks. I think we owe our neighbors a straight explanation, without the talk-radio heat or the social-media hype. Here is part one of two. Start with the U.S. Supreme Court. On April 29, the Court decided a case called Louisiana v. Callais. The vote was 6-3. Justice Samuel Alito wrote the majority opinion. After the 2020 census, Louisiana drew a new congressional map. A federal court said the map likely violated Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, the part of federal law that bans practices that dilute minority voting strength. Louisiana's Legislature then drew a second majority-Black district to fix the problem. A different group of voters sued, saying the new map was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, meaning race had been the main factor in drawing the lines. The Supreme Court agreed with the second group. It ruled that Louisiana was not actually required to draw a second majority-Black district, so race-based map-drawing was not justified. Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act still exists. Anyone telling you the Voting Rights Act is gone is wrong. But the legal test plaintiffs have to pass in these cases is now significantly harder. Basically, the bar moved. Now to Mississippi. We have a related case that has been moving through the federal courts. Our three state Supreme Court districts -- Northern, Central, and Southern -- have not been redrawn since 1987. In August 2025, U.S. District Judge Sharion Aycock, a George W. Bush appointee, ruled those districts violate Section 2, especially the Central District that covers the Delta and Jackson area. She ordered them redrawn. The 2026 regular session of the Legislature ended without a new map. Governor Tate Reeves then called a special session for May 20 to comply with the order before the federal court imposed one. Here is where the story changed. On Monday, May 11, the U.S. Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals vacated Judge Aycock's order and sent the case back to her court for reconsideration under the new Callais standard. The motion to do that was filed jointly by both sides -- the NAACP, ACLU and other plaintiffs on one side, the State of Mississippi on the other. Both agreed the legal ground had shifted under their feet. What does this mean? The order requiring Mississippi to redraw the Supreme Court districts no longer exists. The case is not closed -- Judge Aycock will look at it again under the tougher Callais standard, and the plaintiffs can amend their arguments. As of this writing, it is not clear whether the Governor will still hold the May 20 special session, postpone it, or use the call for other redistricting matters. That is the immediate situation. One Supreme Court ruling. One federal-court order, now vacated. One special session, now cancelled. Three weeks ago this looked like a forced march to redraw judicial districts. Today it looks like the system pumping the brakes to apply new precedent. In part two, I will get into what the Legislature actually has to decide, the louder argument about Mississippi's congressional map, and what all of this might mean for us in Mississippi. “Go back to your own country.”
An insult Donald Trump throws at me almost every single day.
“My country” is America. My home is right here.
This is where I’m a citizen. This is where I’ve lived for decades. This is where my family is. This is where I’ve worked, earned an education, got involved in my community, organized my neighbors, and now represent them in Congress.
But Trump and the MAGA racists know that. They know I’m an American. Their goal is to blur the line as much as possible, to hammer home the idea that if you’re not born here, that if you look differently than them, or belong to a different religion, that you can never be a real American.
That’s the idea that underpins their entire mass deportation regime, which has targeted people like me and used racial profiling to harass, intimidate, detain, and kill people who they don’t think belong in “their” country. **That’s the racist ideology we’re fighting against, not just Trump’s juvenile insults.**
As I absorb these attacks each and every day, while the most powerful man in the world puts a target on my back, I am not afraid. That’s because I have you and our entire movement that stands in solidarity with one another.

name: Gavin Newsom
subject: Folks ... I am worried.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY CAMPAIGN FOR DEMOCRACY PAC
body:
We may have enjoyed our last free and fair election.

| | | | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
Hi there. It's Gavin Newsom. I'm reaching out to respectfully ask you to split a contribution of $35, or whatever you can afford today to the Democratic Parties of Alabama, South Carolina, Tennessee and Louisiana. Please.

Folks ... I am worried. God help us if Republicans are able to re-district their way to a House majority. We may have enjoyed our last free and fair election. First it was Texas, North Carolina and Missouri. Now they are dead-set on erasing Black representation in the South.

I want to stress the importance of this ask. Republicans are ruthless in their pursuit of power, and the only thing that can stop them is us. We have to help Democrats turn up the volume on the Republican scheme or make them pay a price in the polls by taking seats they thought were safe.

If everyone getting this split even $35 between these four state parties, they'd have the resources to build and organize like never before. Remember, these are long-neglected states. Unfortunately, not everyone gives or can give -- so I am personally counting on people who understand the stakes to chip-in what they can today ... before it's too late.

[**If making Republicans pay a price for their redistricting schemes in the South, protecting Black representation, and taking back the House is worth $35 to you, please split that contribution between the Alabama, South Carolina, Louisiana and Tennessee Democratic Parties TODAY.**](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/7771?refcode=em260514&t=1&akid=2946%2E4767699%2EkL554x) Gavin Newsom |

Tlaib recently refused to disavow communist, Muslim streamer Hasan Piker after his calls for Trump's death, instead choosing to label the sitting President a "fascist." Her disgusting response reflects a broader pattern inside the Democratic Party of promoting extreme rhetoric even as the life of President Trump and his supporters are threatened...
Loomer Unleashed asked Tlaib directly:
_" Hey, I was wondering, will you apologize to President Trump for associating with _Hasan _Piker -- an individual who called for Trump's death?"_

_" You want me to apologize to fascist President Trump?"_

This is at least the second time Tlaib has refused to distance herself from Piker's extreme rhetoric. Earlier this month, Tlaib appeared at a campaign rally for Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El Sayed, a fellow Islamist and terrorist sympathizer, who has been closely aligned with Piker's political orbit.
If Democrats take control of Congress in November, there is a credible path for Tlaib to gain significant institutional power, including a potential role in influencing or even leading the House Financial Services Committee. This committee is responsible for overseeing America's banks and financial systems. It's considered a highly desirable position in Washington that gives the chair great power to influence rules and capital flows on Wall Street.
Current Ranking Member "Crazy" Maxine Waters is getting old and may not seek to maintain her leadership role indefinitely. Waters has survived numerous scandals associated with her position on the committee. All involve Waters and her family members making money off her votes. She has been investigated by the House Ethics Committee for bailing out OneUnited Bank, which her husband held stock in. She's also been accused of giving family members over one million dollars through her campaign. Somehow, she has clung to power despite serious red flags about her own conflicts of interest and self-dealing.
Within the Congressional Progressive Caucus, Tlaib holds a [leadership](https://substack.com/redirect/96464fa8-e7e3-4f9d-a560-604650ca4f06?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) position as one of ten Vice Chairs, while Waters is [simply](https://substack.com/redirect/94f6b673-4303-43f3-8545-d2b04e58758f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a rank-and-file member with no formal party leadership role.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1abf4aec-ab1b-417d-8f62-7021077e1e88?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/53f42453-2245-4ebc-a6f7-1baeff091fe0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a1920838-bd28-4286-8000-bd8aeba47807?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Tlaib is also closely aligned with Rep. Ilhan Omar, a fellow Islamist and "Squad" member, who serves as Deputy Chair of the same caucus, making her one of the most influential figures within the progressive wing.
Tlaib and Waters are personally close, making a transfer of power more likely. Tlaib has repeatedly praised Waters as a mentor and political ally. In a January 15, 2019 Politico [interview](https://substack.com/redirect/cb62bd5d-7847-45aa-a847-3f5939658baa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Tlaib called Waters a "shero" and praised her as "unwavering when it comes to holding corporations accountable."

Days later, Tlaib [posted](https://substack.com/redirect/cd3a23e6-cf8e-4aab-a7aa-a89aca0c4a46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): "My new chairwoman right here! @RepMaxineWaters is an unwavering fighter for the people and she will hold the powerful accountable."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2a51a925-fd49-4802-82d3-8770100930c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In her official congressional [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/a2f6c3b5-97e2-40b2-89ee-19a62f387fee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at the time, Tlaib wrote: "It is an honor to have the opportunity to serve on the Financial Services Committee under the leadership of Chairwoman Maxine Waters, someone I deeply admire."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e12108af-b342-4d4f-bd73-4385dcbe3ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
By July 2020, her loyalty was again [displayed](https://substack.com/redirect/65783ca3-660b-4a61-90ca-67c24fe7ab74?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): "I will follow Khalto Maxine anywhere."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0d2e7bba-5973-4fef-a9b5-41dc82817b5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
That loyalty appears to be mutual. In an April 17, 2021 CNN interview, Waters [said](https://substack.com/redirect/beac3bdf-394f-430a-88df-a8fd180f82fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Tlaib: "So she spoke her mind and I appreciate that, and I love her for it."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9867c78e-a532-4b21-bec3-69f794685d25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
If Tlaib were to take control of the Financial Services Committee, the policy implications would yank America's financial system to the left. She has consistently supported aggressive taxation policies and the use of congressional authority to attack political opponents.
In 2020, Tlaib openly backed the [release](https://substack.com/redirect/b9a24a33-7cf8-4a42-84e5-af28ebfe22ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of President Trump's tax returns, accusing him of using "unscrupulous" and potentially illegal tactics.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b5766bb0-f160-448d-8bc4-11cabfd09d7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
She has also pushed for a sweeping wealth tax. In 2023, she [introduced](https://substack.com/redirect/b16a7f0f-1229-4044-9b01-7ef6f56cecd6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the OLIGARCH Act, targeting the ultra-wealthy, arguing that economic inequality justifies increased taxation and government intervention.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d2d26e17-533b-4526-b053-6dafb65f40f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
"Tax the rich. All of them," Tlaib [posted](https://substack.com/redirect/6154ce54-0018-42b7-ab30-584d4a088896?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). There's little daylight between the kinds of Communist "tax the rich" policies Mayor Mamdani is implementing in New York City and Tlaib's vision for the entire U.S.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/53f32bcc-b422-43fa-9ba9-82e0ed430128?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Tlaib's refusal to disavow rhetoric calling for violence, combined with her growing influence inside the Democrat Party, represents a serious threat if she's elevated to Chair of the Financial Services Committee.
The midterms present voters with a stark choice: Tlaib's vision of expanded government control and targeting of political opponents, or a Congress that offers Americans more freedom, more opportunity to take home the money they earn, and support for President Trump's agenda.

subject: One fearless young woman can change everything
body:
For years, the Left thought they had a permanent grip on America's youth.

| | | | [](http://links.stoppingsocialistdems.com/u/click?_t=4dcc2aab65fd4d0da6a107b0eef86d43&_m=32a36301bce6499baf5bc6f4c3be4898&_e=HjO4eR6wicLMzzPB6K81O1jPV14XDeFjkAbdIrbSttk1g52a3iVjnCXb7W2CZY1LJWIwCy_q6j5PmQ66Yn_cvNrEBQYW2OMeePPSLn5lJMKMbGWk3rJAdWy19zm6jsosHy-rVJJspigJwCSk8sW0YzMwXXvIxVu99npqJxJji2paWqaGmG60q6GsvFTxAp85w8aD4h6NZKA7TPMydXvCMH-pMa5e3uXm4ZBQFygjZMO7Rr_vvCuzoUFiDEfoYH8GdD2iAhbEBdBYt0cKc_fx3k_mf9ffGYSxe0mYHK4f7D7B83iWN1sPkgu9DTZ9olnA4hp2ANkPmoI14FlOgr1YlIE91IVMDx7kL6dh7qjX-ZytM3xDBkmOcsbLX4Z_1j6eU_dyTRUiDIITF9c5rlALX9RdLFdVdJQ-y_c2x1D9m4_TyrwY5qA5UbYcVc_0_3LVswDC1uJP6DZYSjAC_CV6LYDIcZWjd9H_w5CEIVMeBefiGlfG1B2FJPe3iHeLmnZkpaJkKjHtdEpkQ3uHKwXFau1bvS1zx0GOFrAALQyfPxgD8qNslUxAtO_jDi1ISvGzJA6rQSfTNoz0BspOU3i8NfrMtbnIkPix4wXMyWWaamUIvvHF8O4ndsD_3f3r3ClP-Ys31eavzwFUdiN_a3AJNHDhAT0doniINxL4YyiudzMjEP1DZsCo8Arjdm8T-FtR)
---
| | | Peter,
---
For years, the Left thought they had a permanent grip on America's youth.

And honestly?

For a while, they did.
They dominated classrooms. Social media. Pop culture. Hollywood. Universities.

They told an entire generation that loving your country was shameful...

That faith was outdated... And traditional values were something to erase.

But thanks to Charlie's leadership, something incredible has happened:

Young men are rejecting the Left in RECORD numbers. High school boys are the most Conservative they've been in 50 years.

And Gen Z is heading back to church -- in numbers greater than their parents' or grandparents' generations.

For the first time in decades, we are WINNING the American Culture War.

**But there 's still one group the Left is desperately fighting to hold onto: **

_America 's young women. _

Because they know something very important, Peter...

If they can win the hearts and minds of young women...

They don't just shape individuals. They shape families. They shape homes. They shape future generations.

**And that 's exactly why Turning Point USA's Women's Leadership Summit (WLS) matters more than ever this year. **
---
[](http://links.stoppingsocialistdems.com/u/click?_t=4dcc2aab65fd4d0da6a107b0eef86d43&_m=32a36301bce6499baf5bc6f4c3be4898&_e=HjO4eR6wicLMzzPB6K81O1jPV14XDeFjkAbdIrbSttk1g52a3iVjnCXb7W2CZY1LJWIwCy_q6j5PmQ66Yn_cvNrEBQYW2OMeePPSLn5lJMKMbGWk3rJAdWy19zm6jsosHy-rVJJspigJwCSk8sW0YzMwXXvIxVu99npqJxJji2paWqaGmG60q6GsvFTxAp85w8aD4h6NZKA7TPMydXvCMH-pMa5e3uXm4ZBQFygjZMN7UXH0cGaMtDWD2ynHVO3I3yF3_oVt1TQ14sGyyRG0yJBWtkhAwnpeqNCzIVdkfyLdl374rF3arj3fbXOllmuIoE9FsMIuGwYsvt07XT9Q-Nwn6UuXhbK9HG7YJiYmIvvRzju_DyGpTLJicQ6QRHDFb0lSyutsX5_O13RyscKU-Y4LPj4fnZ7c45pmOkmAdrFPRKj7GJ3XdeNVaCdDqfEGSkOlpbuSSSP1Qn1eOIIS5z9_tIEwYo7g7L4dakCjBJzYrTsjAZvecBPuYoC34KLh6vKyGH7S5Fc0ztBN0x9mPobp11YXw5iYSFIAiXQgqklkFHj3z77EYyHdihk0Fi3C-tWd5SiC_hVYz4DnhDCpPlr8ycKuKfwIDR_5_Qc7J5chos2LBUwijlXSAuA5TH-UFiJIoQeEHdt1rd1NfA_Tz1ij9keakRrjCzS9QNaKrwn7i0vVkRJMfKiBo-oLC0WK)
---
I've spent the last 7 years helping lead the team behind Turning Point USA's biggest events.

And I can honestly tell you:

I've never seen young women hungrier for truth, purpose, faith, wellness, and real community than they are right now.

Because modern culture is failing them.

The Left sold them confusion and called it "empowerment."

They told young women: femininity is weakness, motherhood is oppression, faith is foolish, patriotism is toxic, and healthy living is extremism.

And after years of hearing those lies...

So many young women feel exhausted. Lonely. Anxious. Spiritually empty.

They're searching for something REAL.

Somewhere they can breathe again. Somewhere they can grow stronger instead of being torn down.

_That 's what Women's Leadership Summit has become. _

Not just another event... but a place where thousands of women come together to rediscover truth, confidence, purpose, and courage.

**From June 5 -7 in San Antonio, women from across the country will gather to: **

✅ Strengthen their minds
✅ Cultivate wellness
✅ Step boldly into their purpose
✅ Anchor their spirits in faith

And when they walk into that room... _Something changes. _
---
[](http://links.stoppingsocialistdems.com/u/click?_t=4dcc2aab65fd4d0da6a107b0eef86d43&_m=32a36301bce6499baf5bc6f4c3be4898&_e=HjO4eR6wicLMzzPB6K81O1jPV14XDeFjkAbdIrbSttk1g52a3iVjnCXb7W2CZY1LJWIwCy_q6j5PmQ66Yn_cvNrEBQYW2OMeePPSLn5lJMKMbGWk3rJAdWy19zm6jsosHy-rVJJspigJwCSk8sW0YzMwXXvIxVu99npqJxJji2paWqaGmG60q6GsvFTxAp85w8aD4h6NZKA7TPMydXvCMH-pMa5e3uXm4ZBQFygjZMOQIiuPFQ5AnVQ6FF6rpzTYIzGXlxdiTDfGaOkGSDvcG5mF4k9tTOsyK81BZvAVa6riplHukNCTx_yB_9gTmn9aSomwtB2dkb9Cpmur4etJry7qRJK59jw2-CQWLl3VKW62RWllOoOZOBaN8EahWE9B8_FYqrjP1QAZs25-xsDG2mkYO6mg--TTH8lhhEVpOGfXteVerbeEYSlynNnAF6EAdk7kFCvfXa1cLrEVttFMjsh-UHsxetOoUFmOpH8E-d4Aj4PU7qjocIKQvJnFAU9Yk1yGsrCmjcPrgFs4Zo7oDWFGDj7J0orLSDso6wuK3uFSV6mCs5l1gYtoTTyS8JpjSz-w6YhcBrLrwGjdkG4JKeQMGcchug9O35ou0gtOqM-6ip4dg1EMZ6cJveaB6iU_67X6V1BeONfUFEfJgy26q6iROtfBbVPdiM5_v27AYMBg1HzrPjHog8DJE9edwAe6)
---
Peter, I see it happen every year -- and from backstage, you can actually watch the change happen in real time.

Young women arriving unsure of themselves...

_Then leaving with fire in their eyes. _

Women who thought they were alone suddenly realizing:

_" There are thousands of other women who love God, love Freedom, and LOVE AMERICA just like I do." _

That matters.

Because the Left wants these young women isolated.

Disconnected. Demoralized. Easy to manipulate.

But WLS reminds them they are part of something MUCH bigger.

**A movement. A sisterhood. A generation of strong, patriotic women rising up to reject the lies they 've been fed for years. **

And these women don't just leave inspired... _They go home ready to LEAD. _

I've watched women leave WLS and:

🔥 Strengthen their faith
🔥 Embrace their femininity
🔥 Build friendships rooted in truth and purpose
🔥 Boldly speak out on their campuses
🔥 Launch Turning Point USA chapters
🔥 Lead in their communities and in this movement

This is how we WIN the culture war. One fearless young woman at a time.
---
[](http://links.stoppingsocialistdems.com/u/click?_t=4dcc2aab65fd4d0da6a107b0eef86d43&_m=32a36301bce6499baf5bc6f4c3be4898&_e=HjO4eR6wicLMzzPB6K81O1jPV14XDeFjkAbdIrbSttk1g52a3iVjnCXb7W2CZY1LJWIwCy_q6j5PmQ66Yn_cvNrEBQYW2OMeePPSLn5lJMKMbGWk3rJAdWy19zm6jsosHy-rVJJspigJwCSk8sW0YzMwXXvIxVu99npqJxJji2paWqaGmG60q6GsvFTxAp85w8aD4h6NZKA7TPMydXvCMH-pMa5e3uXm4ZBQFygjZMNa0R25vHvgBK_gesiRhdS0dOfQYnnJnoBz1zudhkGCrG_hrwY3tMaCSsV8r1HtO8_grhbCMZuLEGp5r2nHVgGZewbfZqPjuyGB7aYUyM32meqEoywlm1LxoKalyC8DPTOUxN5SHhYZicedjqG-lsOIfLjPJTY-4k6qpS8Zan7e6DHVl_kWCoNyJQy2pnibROn_sw9KXj1dFb2jjhTsr_MtFhh7REUND22dXZpUMqFwrvOYf40XVK4SXjLFYWRqbENfikF5F3rvjTPm3-HaxMo7hdJ5UjHtCCVNxqpSRwE-3C_kJKN-ZLj9DUE3r5WeKxGWZlgMnRMzQLOnqNYbm-d9ZFLxFXNaQS-pzmbWTkLGshl8q-bieE3fvyKYezbGxZ6rz43VrLvwO2Dzs6vjrDc3sKnWWJVcUt2YEaXnpqpvOWn3ybIzvhjOPx7jZfQ6x4VrsvSlfAYSu47KAXrCKAgU)
---
_But here 's the problem, Peter... _

Right now, we have many young women who desperately want to attend WLS but may miss this life-changing experience without help.

Some are students working to save enough money for gas or airfare.

Others are trapped in environments where they constantly feel pressured to stay silent about their beliefs.

**And many just need ONE place where they can be surrounded by women who will encourage them, strengthen them, and remind them they were created for MORE. **

_But there 's not much time left before the doors open... _

**Boysko Bulletin: Historic Win - Paid Family and Medical Leave for Virginians!**
---
Dear Peter, I was thrilled to stand with my colleague Delegate Sewell and Governor Spanberger to celebrate the signing of our legislation, my bill [**SB2**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131388633/620929482/-793872083?e=a5fd1f8bfb&c2id=ad4a75795cd24cdd0805bc6221080b7c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMTJiNzNjOTgtYTg0Zi1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ACMCT2CPOOYU7fwwET2q0u9RxWra7UbXdHAIoES1QW0=&emci=227d1a47-543f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=12b73c98-a84f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=22486556), and Delegate Briana Sewell’s [**HB1207**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131388634/620929491/309082057?e=a5fd1f8bfb&c2id=ad4a75795cd24cdd0805bc6221080b7c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMTJiNzNjOTgtYTg0Zi1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ACMCT2CPOOYU7fwwET2q0u9RxWra7UbXdHAIoES1QW0=&emci=227d1a47-543f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=12b73c98-a84f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=22486556). With benefits set to begin in 2028, Virginia is the 14th state plus the District of Columbia, notably the first in the South, to establish a Paid Family and Medical Leave program, expanding access to more than 3.5 million Virginians who currently lack access to paid leave. I’ve been working on this policy as the Senate’s Chief Patron for the past 8 legislative sessions to get it right for Virginia because in households all over Virginia, families face medical emergencies and welcome new children. For those lucky enough to have paid family and medical leave through their employer—or enough personal savings to get by during unpaid time off—serious health events, caring for a parent at the end of their lives, or the arrival of a new baby can be manageable and meaningful, with the focus on healing and bonding. But for most Virginians, these life events come with an impossible choice: care for a loved one, recover from a medical crisis, bond with a newborn—or keep working to afford rent, groceries, utilities, and other basic needs. I draw from my own experience when my husband and I welcomed our second child delivered 2 months early and she had to spend 6 weeks in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit in a hospital more than 20 miles from our home. My husband had to go back to work within 2 weeks of the medical crisis because we could not afford to have him take any unpaid time away. It was extremely difficult for me to manage alone. Now, nearly 30 years later, families will have the grace to care for themselves or each other during serious events without having to worry about going bankrupt. Benefits start in December of 2028. The paid family and medical leave program provides up to 12 weeks of job-protected, paid leave at 80% of wages, capped at the state average weekly wage. It’s a universal program so that roughly 3.5 million working Virginians will be covered when they are welcoming a new baby, caring for themselves or a loved one during a serious illness, welcoming a loved one in the military back home after being in combat, or when a parent needs care at the end of their life. Our bill also gives grace to those who need paid leave because of a dangerous domestic situation. Did you know that among developed economies, the United States is the only country that does not guarantee paid maternity leave in the world? Small businesses support paid family and medical leave programs - it is the most affordable way to provide benefits to their employees, allowing them to compete with larger companies. My bill offers a special benefit to employers of 10 or fewer employees - there is no employer contribution to the fund. Everyone should have that grace when they or their loved ones need care during these most profound life events. SB 2 makes that a reality for Virginia’s working families. I thank my Chief of Staff Karen Harrison, who has been the bedrock keeping this momentum moving forward for nearly a decade, the many stakeholders especially Freedom Virginia our state partners over the past 3 years, the Campaign For a Family Friendly Economy, who started the groundwork in 2018, our brothers and sisters in the labor community and our national stakeholders who have worked with me all 8 sessions, and all of my colleagues who have supported this legislation consistently over the years. Kindest regards,
