clean_body: The biggest National Memorial Day Parade yet It's Gary Sinise here. | | | | Friend, It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250th birthday. Friend, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. Friend, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you. WWII veterans were a key part of the first parade when it was revived in 2005, as they have been every year since for the last 20 years. But this may be the last year we have the opportunity to have these brave men and women with us for the parade. | | | | | | | | This year is a rare moment when living witnesses to World War II and America 's 250th birthday overlap. Imagine this: It's a dark night in Newark, New Jersey. A young officer, just 26 years old, father of four, races to back up his brothers in blue. A dangerous chase unfolds – armed thugs in a speeding car, weaving through streets at 70 mph the wrong way, endangering innocent families. These criminals point a loaded semi-automatic right at Officer Jovanny Crespo's face. They try to mow him down like roadkill. In a split-second decision, the kind no desk-jockey prosecutor could ever understand, Officer Crespo acts to protect himself, his fellow officers, and the public. He stops the threat. Lives are saved. But what does he get in return? Handcuffs. Indictment. A sham trial where he's branded a "murderer" and "killer" by radicals who hate the badge. | [Help Free JOVANNY](http://links.standingstrongamerica.com/u/click?_t=29c3b6e742c849fabbcc130432510e66&_m=bf52e99ce2d249df9b5558ffa64bb028&_e=auFGpb4g7oAau5UFuyjjH0PGhFRwy9a3nRUkSikRTXGXWaPeLeaS_8Sfzm8x__irYsl8mWELsSbr7WCxWqwTE38Ssak1-GcE_CAHmdq_bZ4ub_Wm-VDtlzXusqOc0db4d8cEA-iOePKdRwcThBBWBSENyW08xa4N1VpKZTJPIddPzUgIYyMBSKVoNuGYUNVY_INQ5SLz9A3fNIEv3YppwkIYRk9LIOhVRVP_fY0bcL1Bvy-R_HnpLa1VC6Q3BM289qMU6E1Cj1yEl76izegvST-BIvomxnIRMklHG_LJvivoq_fLer4oUBujtcb3yqv2oa3hNS6z51Ji8acERdfAQQa5d3VChFnHkXgs771BiOpHXuDa7l_L6vuo0oFwS0oJ9fa02sVt8KlCfSYAavtP1T_QRtlbjoRCk6tHi-D7Gthe1SQxRLAG5eVLBwgonVKc)

In 2018, "The Squad" was dismissed by many Democrats as a fringe coalition of loud, radical freshmen from New York, Michigan, and Minnesota. Eight years later, the movement they helped build now dominates the ideological direction of the Democrat Party.
From wealth taxes, anti-Israel activism, to the weaponization of government against President Trump, the once-fringe socialist, grievance-driven agenda of Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Rashida Tlaib, Ilhan Omar, and their communist and Islamic allies has become mainstream Democrat orthodoxy.
But, that doesn't explain why this transformation happened so quickly. Behind the scenes sits BerlinRosen, one of the most influential Democrat consulting and communications firms in the country.
The firm was co-founded by longtime Bill de Blasio confidant [Jonathan Rosen](https://substack.com/redirect/555fcbcf-8431-44e9-87e6-4c2c963fc39d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [Valerie Berlin](https://substack.com/redirect/c4f0e79a-6371-4301-843d-c9fb2ee4c8de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a longtime ally of New York City Comptroller Brad Lander, who is himself closely aligned with New York's socialist mayor Zohran Mamdani. BerlinRosen's influence extends far beyond local politics. Its parent company, Orchestra, employs top Democrat power brokers, including former Obama campaign manager and Kamala Harris adviser [David Plouffe](https://substack.com/redirect/e2eb28e1-f3fc-489c-abf5-51efd0603ef1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

| This cup of coffee could shake up the political establishment.
Seriously.
Before I decided to run for Congress, I was an attorney, but I left that line of work because I couldn't keep watching billionaires, corporations, and career politicians make life harder for working people while pretending nothing could be done about it.
For the last year, I've been working part-time as a barista while running for Congress against an incumbent who's taken millions of dollars in corporate PAC money and who has been in office longer than I've been alive. In 30 years, she's only passed two bills.
I don't know about you, but I would not get away with that at my job.
Denver deserves a representative who knows what it feels like when rent is too high, health care is too expensive, wages are not keeping up, and billionaires are buying our government out from under us, because they've lived it too.
That's why I'm running. No corporate PAC money or checks from the billionaire oligarchy. No money from private equity firms jacking up rents or health insurance companies profiting off our pain.
Just people chipping in what they can because they believe politics should answer to us.

But Republicans have a different playbook: If they lose, they try to throw out votes, rewrite the rules, or cancel the results.

Now they are trying it again in Georgia.

Georgia Supreme Court Justice Sarah Warren is on the ballot against Jen Jordan on May 19. And when Warren was asked whether she would rule out using a legal loophole to let Republicans nullify the results if she loses, **_she refused to answer._**

clean_body: Republicans tried this in North Carolina. Now Georgia is next. | = Peter, when you lose an election, you leave office (or you never take it in the first place). That is how democracy works. But Republicans have a different playbook: If they lose, they try to throw out votes, rewrite the rules, or cancel the results. We saw it in North Carolina, when Republicans tried to overturn Justice Allison Riggs’ win because they did not like the outcome. That is not just being a sore loser — that's attacking the foundations of the democratic process. Now they are trying it again in Georgia. Georgia Supreme Court Justice Sarah Warren is on the ballot against Jen Jordan on May 19. And when Warren was asked whether she would rule out using a legal loophole to let Republicans nullify the results if she loses, she refused to answer. = | = This should be simple: If Sarah Warren loses, Jen Jordan should take office. But Republicans keep showing us who they are. When voters reject them, they try to find another way to hold onto power. Our extraordinary EMILYs List community helped stop them in North Carolina. Now we need to do it again in Georgia. The Democratic Party of Georgia Judicial Fund is funding the paid media program to make sure voters know what is at stake before Election Day on May 19. Jen Jordan and Miracle Rankin can win — but they need the resources to fight back now. Please make a split donation between EMILYs List and the Democratic Party of Georgia Judicial Fund to help elect Jen Jordan and Miracle Rankin to the Georgia Supreme Court: = Republicans should not get to overturn elections just because they don’t like the outcome. We’re now hearing reports that President Donald Trump is considering an executive order declaring a so-called “emergency” to seize greater federal authority over elections.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260514em [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260514em]
FIGHT BACK [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260514em]
This is deeply alarming to say the least.
But you don’t have to take my word for it: Our founders were explicit about this. They had just fought a king. They understood that concentrating too much power in one person was dangerous. That’s why the Constitution divides authority and states administer elections.
That’s why no president — no matter how loud or how desperate — gets to override the system because he’s afraid of losing.
As Oregon’s Secretary of State, I oversee our elections. I take an oath to the Constitution — not to any president. And I will stand up to any administration that tries to abuse emergency powers to interfere with Oregon’s voting systems or intimidate our election workers.
But I need your help to keep up the fight in light of Trump’s illegal actions, which is why I’m reaching out today. Can I count on you to join me in this fight against President Trump’s lawlessness by chipping in $5, $10, or more right away? Communicating this threat to Oregonians statewide requires resources. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260514em]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260514em]
We’ve already beaten back federal overreach in court before. When attempts were made to stretch authority beyond its limits, Oregon pushed back — and won.
If we have to do it again, we will.
But defending democracy requires a strong grassroots team prepared to meet the fight head-on — and that’s where you come in.
If you believe, as I do, that no president should be able to manufacture an emergency to grab control over elections, I’m asking you to stand with me. Please contribute today to help us protect Oregon’s elections and hold President Trump accountable before it’s too late. >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260514em]
Thank you,
Tobias Read

See link below_ Akayla Gardner is an excellent reporter and White House correspondent for MSNOW (MSNBC). And as you may have seen this week,[ ](https://default.salsalabs.org/T4635e169-72c1-4cdc-9d15-0f2210505664/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)**[she’s not afraid](https://default.salsalabs.org/T9a4617f2-f9ee-481a-8479-479122ca9505/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) to push back against Trump and his lies.** Donald Trump, a chronic jerk, berated Gardner for asking an entirely fair question and correctly pointing out his obvious lie about his ballroom project. _“You wanted [Federal Reserve Chair] Jerome Powell fired for cost overruns,” Gardner pointed out to Trump, referring to the Fed’s ongoing renovation project of its Washington headquarters. “How is that different than your ballroom and the reflecting pool?”_ _“What happened is that we have a ballroom that’s under budget,” Trump replied. “It’s going up right here. I’ve doubled the size of it because we obviously need that, and we’re right now on budget, under budget, and ahead of schedule.”_[This is bullsh*t] _“The price has doubled,” Gardner pointed out._ _Trump snapped back: “I doubled the size of it, you dumb person. You are not a smart person.” ([source](https://default.salsalabs.org/T7fc8ad86-e67c-4fc1-8f37-6ce0384bf84f/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9))_ Trump lies as casually as most people breathe, and Gardner did exactly what good reporters are supposed to do: calmly, firmly, and publicly push back with facts. **[This is the kind of courage](https://default.salsalabs.org/T20813e79-01f6-4ef6-9b48-cb014bc3e6d6/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) that is in short supply these days, with far too many people too afraid (perhaps understandably) to get in his path.** And for that, she deserves [thanks](https://default.salsalabs.org/T419df460-2963-4b0a-8d8d-037a49db2428/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9), not abuse. **[Please add your name, and thank her. “Thank you, Akayla Gardner, for standing strong against Trump’s lies.”](https://default.salsalabs.org/T5ef6deb8-14d9-4004-99d6-d628d926bd3c/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)**

subject: A reporter called what we did historic. Here's the full story.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Yen Bailey for Congress
body:
Friend,

Something happened this week that hasn't happened in over 100 years in North Florida, and I want to make sure you know about it.

Yen Bailey just became the only candidate in Florida's 2nd Congressional District to qualify for the ballot by petition. Not by writing a check. By earning it: door by door, county by county, conversation by conversation.

We submitted more than 4,000 signatures from voters across all 16 counties in this district. Democrats, Republicans, and independents. People who are tired of being ignored and ready for something different.

The Tallahassee Democrat called it historic.( https://us.list-manage.com/14x3J09wazJ?e=58216231a8&c2id=8df47a7be007db4a464e6070248494ca). Yahoo News picked it up. And today, we're telling the full story on Daily Kos, because this isn't just a campaign milestone. It's proof that grassroots organizing still works, even in a district they said couldn't be won.

Read the full story here: https://us.list-manage.com/5DLOAWZ3gF7?e=58216231a8&c2id=8df47a7be007db4a464e6070248494ca

If you found it worth reading, take 30 seconds to help us spread it. Comment, recommend, and share the article on Daily Kos. Every recommend helps push this story in front of thousands of new readers across the country who need to hear what's happening in North Florida.

If this campaign has shown you anything, it's that we don't take the easy road. We took the harder one, because that's what this district deserves.

name: Jim Jordan
subject: I’ll never accuse you of abandoning us
body:
No one should ever accuse you of being a Democrat
After all you’ve done for our Party, I salute you, Patriot!

| Patriot,
---
I’m sick of seeing text messages that accuse you of abandoning the GOP after all you’ve done for us.
All because you didn’t give $15 before some random deadline, that’s supposed to mean you **_“betrayed”_** the Republican Party and became a Democrat?
So all the times you stood in line to vote, you knocked on doors, you put up a yard sign, you made phone calls, you filled out surveys, you sacrificed your time and money – suddenly, all of that means nothing?
**_Give me a break! That’s just insulting._**
_Hand to God, I will never stoop to that low._
Truth be told, I try not to write too many emails and texts as it is. I’m busy working in Washington to do the job you asked me to do.
Honestly, fundraising just isn’t Priority #1.
At the end of 2024, I transferred $2.5 MILLION _**away**_ from my own campaign to help conservatives in tough races who _truly_ needed help.
**You know what I care about most?** The _ONLY_ thing that WINS elections – **_VOTES_**.
_That means registering voters, verifying every Trump voter’s profile, and constantly getting LIVE feedback from voters like you so that the President and I _always_ have the best, most accurate data in the country._
That’s how we won in 2024. And it’s my plan to win AGAIN in 2026.

Fellow Conservative,

As a former Navy SEAL I’ve been shot at, blown up, and tested in ways most people never experience. While these lies are annoying and slightly comical, they are a different kind of ugly in this battle for the US Senate.

_**It’s the kind of sleazy politics that makes you wonder how low some people will go just to win.**_

I’ve been in this Minnesota Senate race for roughly a year. I’m still not a household name, but something is clearly shifting. Voters across the state are noticing — _**we’ve now won 13 separate straw polls.**

_[](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=5837efe17c9044bd8e2b232b4a7aaaf7&_e=6Sw6csjH7z-Q1eIc1SSLUhsOSdRk19DqXkjrVUsFM4nwMeRDbo8WOxMFDBEOkIorCR6d_vfxW_YpONqIYxuKcwCBO26E0IHU_aNftho8Ox0x2Ffu97_a19P8qoAc1t3bIDgK2wUNA-ZhwEdMX9vSeu71gBfDtqnT3oRqxjvmWGG50z8sm6gdaTnNlfxligT046_q-LedKyUuKKy13B4gYSCtBtmUA3TGD_TzzAf5SIcHINhHAwD1QWvf8kqXDsxGPHB2dnWbD60_NYejopSA349yeKIP2EHDqPErirCiPbbz9O2jSErQE6kFcasj__6DH4JLTyblhoO-0azU6NMJfZLj02ZnPUMAVx6ZLgQpTmURZj0_smNxrhTcYojyTM8loEB6rdduCvdvGv26JtnzE8MwmcHYtLpENtIuhIWrZDGN6mgiTaP6QREyqdIeA_GLTC8_UvMWgkfO86NQJLJ3uDLaNGOTOOR1Qe18aOOIEsK61BSNG1GwUFvW8Dqs6MGkXsgGnbhBPvcKhfpVrq9hKniHmOw0VOPXeyyDmIDN8NxDz_k9-1zCGtyN696ZKAm9RC2Mv2rTaZQ2fpApVdFrgJXg5PWbUyxE11Egmbt1rB9-1oRLJo0jPVHwnRvfKqHKTt1dt6kjOyEC1Kr3eBb7wkg_fvxXaa71PqAUZ3AY2cYmvXw3ijNm5VwfpPPlIseZvtqBCWHFJtvuO_1-Hby0XS8OsKp4tl6c5F5OTqPNzozdsdtrqvASAtlwhlbWfUH4)_ _
**I always figured the attacks would come eventually. I just didn’t expect them to get this personal or this dishonest this quickly.**

Look, I can handle the incoming fire. I’ve taken harder hits in my life. What I can’t accept is watching a critical Senate seat slip away because my opponents would rather sling mud than talk about the future of this country.

_**This seat is too important to let personal attacks decide who serves Minnesota and who helps stop the radical Democratic agenda in Washington.**_

clean_body: My momentum in the Minnesota Senate race is picking up fast — and that’s exactly why my opponents just launched their nastiest attacks yet. | Fellow Conservative, As a former Navy SEAL I’ve been shot at, blown up, and tested in ways most people never experience. While these lies are annoying and slightly comical, they are a different kind of ugly in this battle for the US Senate. It’s the kind of sleazy politics that makes you wonder how low some people will go just to win. I’ve been in this Minnesota Senate race for roughly a year. I’m still not a household name, but something is clearly shifting. Voters across the state are noticing — we’ve now won 13 separate straw polls. I always figured the attacks would come eventually. I just didn’t expect them to get this personal or this dishonest this quickly. Look, I can handle the incoming fire. I’ve taken harder hits in my life. What I can’t accept is watching a critical Senate seat slip away because my opponents would rather sling mud than talk about the future of this country. This seat is too important to let personal attacks decide who serves Minnesota and who helps stop the radical Democratic agenda in Washington. That’s why I’m asking: You may never have heard of me before, and you might not even live in Minnesota — that’s okay. Here’s the truth: I’m not running for the Senate to build a network for some future lobbying gig or private-sector payday. I’m running because America gave me every chance I’ve ever had, and hanging up my uniform didn’t mean I stopped serving. I still have plenty of fight left in me. But That’s why I’m reaching out to fellow patriots like you. For far too many people – especially Gen Zers like me – owning a car is _too damn expensive_. And things have only gotten worse since Trump and House Republicans started making the price of gas, car insurance, and _literally everything else_ skyrocket.

That’s part of why Americans took over 8.1 _billion_ trips on public transit in 2025, almost half a billion more than the year before.

**But right now, public transit services aren’t meeting the demand.** Across the country (including in Florida), public transit is often slow, late, and unreliable.

When a bus doesn’t show up or is hours late, that’s someone missing work, a class, or a doctor’s appointment. I refuse to accept that’s “just how it is” – **so I’m doing something about it.**

**I introduced the[ _Faster Buses Better Futures Act](http://clicksp.frostforcongress.com/f/a/gm0mn6LIEaekBpeXlwfhig~~/AAPPABA~/SDPlloIn3-MWSHcXiQBhYMY8hG24F5GhyuKOIUhh56IZAyEsXCnNnEMg3fRC6_8TAlWXI-61vDVAezOtYwM7nYUxO7jjeX8LbqBYmy_oHUQ1NXo8H4ukobJfNNGPuLhBrPq0O8p1jcT7WbOVG5x08zjjfusRXCDs2RcnJd6W7ahNIJpKV2migfBrSDCi9ywzgx-S3jU41x6P9YFeq_3CwwvNi-RScDaLGu2oETpgnLD6tQG529kJ1kA6fNt0ye3qeHBrvuw6nwntfOa95tPOvAjCjKty6oe_T448880cBBlmWg1NJMDAYcXOaz2OEXItrnJ2nGE9K-IFd354BURv4dbji57TZKHS8CsSiDPS7YlA_NuvlGGPQ8TrKqGveLhXVCIgjD1aeexG0Yppms96rNKUDZo8McuF2uDM6BrzXpp3JRkh_bhMf8LxFCYaWIV1Sp2Gy1b-UiWlznzIQACic64mUwG103VXwLLKrrL3scs~)_ , which would give money to local transit agencies that are doing their jobs right: making your commute as quick, easy, and safe as possible.**

Better buses reduce traffic congestion, improve our daily commutes, and even provide better air quality with less emissions from cars. Simply put, when buses work better, everybody wins.

But we know that progress like this doesn’t happen without a fight.

Powerful special interests are standing in the way of bold transit policy, and they don’t want people like me (who dare to actually fight for our basic needs) challenging them in Congress.

**That’s why your grassroots support today is so important – it allows us to keep pushing forward, to keep organizing, and keep me in this fight for progress.[_So please, can you donate to my campaign so I can keep fighting to fix our broken transit system in Florida and across the country? >>_**](http://clicksp.frostforcongress.com/f/a/Y__1vzTTjRVgTkhZFO4wWw~~/AAPPABA~/hxDmEA90ls2YyPebsxNOYrhsRTzFy0jFcrG3XEvAphUO0ed2QwRvVnElVzIXAIn09R3hx3kPNeajpSGaF9ux-1N7_iiZC_uBk357sy3ZGNWZjRDm7myalGu3dvIG6jYam06XHVb90i3jjwMLRzwPs3XVWRYjoFI2z7HBvC5vYpW8zNUdyaoRiDbIu8-TJ5ySaZZ7ZTGYBiwagEl_LSvoaZtRnOQ-LYqItgJvicTLQVlk1fmkVvRQ9JeoCpKxmvBQEI7VujhgG6UpBC-SOuzVG2oRjc7H8e17PnHo59j6H0rWBc-OyFH2cpohf34Iqv5jNE_pHE_V4PhEQhh-w2lDDchC_7I66EMj8iZaV9xSWO4~)

name: Jim Jordan
subject: I’ll never accuse you of abandoning us
body:
No one should ever accuse you of being a Democrat
After all you’ve done for our Party, I salute you, Patriot!

| Patriot,
---
I’m sick of seeing text messages that accuse you of abandoning the GOP after all you’ve done for us.
All because you didn’t give $15 before some random deadline, that’s supposed to mean you **_“betrayed”_** the Republican Party and became a Democrat?
So all the times you stood in line to vote, you knocked on doors, you put up a yard sign, you made phone calls, you filled out surveys, you sacrificed your time and money – suddenly, all of that means nothing?
**_Give me a break! That’s just insulting._**
_Hand to God, I will never stoop to that low._
Truth be told, I try not to write too many emails and texts as it is. I’m busy working in Washington to do the job you asked me to do.
Honestly, fundraising just isn’t Priority #1.
At the end of 2024, I transferred $2.5 MILLION _**away**_ from my own campaign to help conservatives in tough races who _truly_ needed help.
**You know what I care about most?** The _ONLY_ thing that WINS elections – **_VOTES_**.
_That means registering voters, verifying every Trump voter’s profile, and constantly getting LIVE feedback from voters like you so that the President and I _always_ have the best, most accurate data in the country._
That’s how we won in 2024. And it’s my plan to win AGAIN in 2026.

body:
What’s happening in court today:
---
Derek, there’s been some movement in our lawsuits against the Trump administration, so I wanted to fill you in. Back in March, we sued the Trump administration under the Freedom of Information Act to demand transparency about their plans for the midterm elections after the Trump administration flat-out _ignored_ our FOIA requests. Now, the Trump administration and their lawyers are trying to dodge accountability again, filing a motion to strike parts of our lawsuit. **They’re refusing to fully answer our suit and calling our allegations “fanciful” and “impertinent.”** I want to be clear, Derek: We’ve got our foot on the gas, and we’re not letting up. The American people deserve to know if the Trump administration is going to attempt to stop their voices from being heard this November. This isn’t our only suit against the administration. Far from it. One more example: We’re also suing to stop President Trump’s new executive order that directs the federal government to build an eligible voter list for each state and instructs the US Postal Service not to return mail ballots for anyone who isn’t on this list. **We have a hearing in that case today.** While our legal team works every day to protect our nation's fundamental principles in court, the DNC is fighting back in every arena. We have organizers on the ground in battleground states registering new Democrats to vote. Teams of experts working to raise money and invest it where it matters most. Communications and social media teams are working to make sure that in big moments, **Americans are hearing from Democrats.** To continue all of this work, we need someone else: you. body:
| | |
**This is a longer email, Peter, but we hope you’ll take a moment to read it because what’s happening to voting rights across the South couldn’t be more important.** What the Supreme Court just did in _Louisiana v. Callais_ is a serious attack on Black political power and voting rights across the South — and Southern organizers are already fighting back against the politicians trying to use this ruling to silence our communities. **[Add your name now to stand in solidarity with organizers resisting voter suppression, gerrymandering, and attacks on our political power.](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoe1DuqQbjt4KoloTZxD-XRKNLGpiR8kOXONBw5-4WsJILVFDr43MZpzEDBi8GFz9xoETCL2SwtSTe3AaqGYldN0L-6U8uk9q7KUI3gYZom6h5q4w0mRL9dWZxUkIZmvjGmdRbZ82gP08Lz45TS8-dmn80C6-4xU-wHpZUqM7d2PfBFI_ZQG-TinSHSPHT7BIhT5EMss3HacXlVRE_FgK8Umq5aYs9KdniNNOsjw7alyzi_NrmlvVR19LsKF4_iipFKfhTpsB8D7450_qjO2ZPC0mWvbFdfZfhEbiG0Rd_wlQ8X95gHBGAt8vPPQR1a3gDd2brHp5gujLMOiUDpCC_OfhUHkWu5dc60LPLbHvKxoEJt1ggOGzks2Au-_Zo7pEHw/4qm/_mNPNYhPSZWF8-F68Gf39w/h0/h001.IVCw0O-Y9tko7M1pHMUP_gKbM-TBhxa2t5yzGHUkxnU)** **[Sign the petition »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoe1DuqQbjt4KoloTZxD-XRKNLGpiR8kOXONBw5-4WsJILVFDr43MZpzEDBi8GFz9xoETCL2SwtSTe3AaqGYldN0L-6U8uk9q7KUI3gYZom6h5q4w0mRL9dWZxUkIZmvjGmdRbZ82gP08Lz45TS8-dmn80C6-4xU-wHpZUqM7d2PffRD-vtcsNavHRI12GsOHzUgjQpbAnCLal3697rExeAGcu0lx3GtbZlYiAPWgHDBt9VXHPwIo2X90PuHQaml9pfMa4uHndMDJpRR4JngJ3uGV1NmDWN-iIqY5mUen35S5VjJef0c3eTmXeF25Cz5yBPmJ010CwvO8H4r7k2ZnQZPcM7cxeXiKnnwSGiVgUQeAMCZ46ocjKHKYjvABnaJ-bg/4qm/_mNPNYhPSZWF8-F68Gf39w/h1/h001.ZQgMa8U2HdACSkKZqusMENWmIX9y8OzxxsA2YRvpPq8)** Peter, My name is **Britney Whaley** , and I’m the Southeast Regional Director for the Working Families Party. I’m also a Black Southern organizer who has spent decades watching our communities fight for the right to be heard, represented, and treated like full participants in this democracy. **So when I tell you that what happened with the Supreme Court’s decision in _Louisiana v. Callais_****is serious, I need you to understand that for those of us in the South, this isn’t abstract. We know exactly what this means because we’ve lived through versions of it before.** ICYMI, here’s what this case was about: after years of organizing and legal challenges from Black voters in Louisiana, the state was finally required to create a second majority-Black congressional district so Black communities would have a fair chance at representation. Black people make up nearly one-third of Louisiana’s population, but for years were locked out of political power through manipulated district maps. **Now, with the _Louisiana v. Callais_****decision, the Supreme Court has opened the door to unraveling those protections altogether.** What that means in plain language is that politicians can once again redraw districts to dilute Black voting power while pretending these attacks are “race-neutral.” It means protections under the Voting Rights Act are hanging by a thread. And it means states across the South are already moving quickly to eliminate districts where Black communities have finally gained representation. **This is not hypothetical.** Tennessee has already used this ruling as political cover to continue reshaping its maps — including moves that threaten and weaken Black political representation in Memphis, home to the state’s only majority-Black congressional district. Other Southern states are already preparing challenges, redraws, and power grabs of their own in Georgia, Alabama, Mississippi, Texas, and North Carolina. **And we need to be honest about what this really is.** The same political forces stripping Black communities of voting power are the same forces making it harder for poor and working-class people to survive across the South. They are attacking unions, underfunding schools and hospitals, criminalizing protest, gutting worker protections, banning books, targeting immigrants, and keeping wages low while corporations and billionaires hoard wealth and power. **Because they understand something our movements have always understood too: when Black people, working-class people, immigrants, young people, poor people, and multiracial communities organize together, they threaten minority rule.** The history of the South — and especially the history of Black Southern organizing — teaches us that the fight for voting rights has always been connected to the fight for economic justice, labor rights, dignity, and self-determination. The people who marched for voting rights were also fighting for fair wages, housing, healthcare, public education, and the right for ordinary people to have a say over the conditions of their lives. This has never been just about symbolism or representation alone. **It’s about whether we will build a democracy that works for the many instead of a wealthy and powerful minority desperately trying to cling to control by any means necessary.** The Voting Rights Act itself was dreamed and built from marches, organizing meetings, church basements, labor struggles, freedom schools, and jail cells. It came from ordinary Black people in the South risking everything because they believed democracy should belong to all of us. And ever since Shelby County v. Holder gutted the Voting Rights Act, this Court has been slowly tearing those protections apart while hoping the rest of the country wouldn’t notice until it was too late. **But here’s what else I know: the South has never stopped fighting back.** The same South they try to paint as backwards and hopeless is the same South that built some of the most powerful freedom movements this country has ever seen. In spite of repression, voter suppression, violence, and disinvestment, ordinary people organized anyway. Our communities are always making a way out of no way. They can redraw districts. But they can’t erase us. And they can’t stop organized people who know their history, know their communities, and know their power. **That’s why the Working Families Party is joining faith leaders, organizers, and movement partners from across the South for a Moral Moment for Voting Rights on May 16 in Alabama.** Right now, we’re asking people across the country to stand in solidarity with Southern organizers fighting to defend voting rights and democracy. **[Add your name to our solidarity petition today and stand with our folks who are fighting back against voter suppression, gerrymandering, and attacks on our political power.](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoe1DuqQbjt4KoloTZxD-XRKNLGpiR8kOXONBw5-4WsJILVFDr43MZpzEDBi8GFz9xoETCL2SwtSTe3AaqGYldN0L-6U8uk9q7KUI3gYZom6h5q4w0mRL9dWZxUkIZmvjGjwyXcNebEomWUXNXalLBR8r212qduxa8tensFUWS75dDaG2jxdVTo5h14uOGTiovGctMxdSU98qbvN2bYzZxMqe5bn7fUy1vrIH0pDGUiuT9-YjfLThOwT5Y72KzKzhcva4Mi9wq6gv9QZwdnyXCQr-VdOihWODkUDoJ7AUGqXpNWLqYKj8Lyhd7MrSc0RkSKsrU5bV4HRJh0gTSplbj8r3fuLPCFyEdobYowRzgRno/4qm/_mNPNYhPSZWF8-F68Gf39w/h2/h001.sgATNvPMo__QODo5KYp4a666k54Gup19cfSS4VUOuoQ)** **** **[Sign the petition](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoe1DuqQbjt4KoloTZxD-XRKNLGpiR8kOXONBw5-4WsJILVFDr43MZpzEDBi8GFz9xoETCL2SwtSTe3AaqGYldN0L-6U8uk9q7KUI3gYZom6h5q4w0mRL9dWZxUkIZmvjGjwyXcNebEomWUXNXalLBR8Y7Dj1bxK5vzJEE2DJkfwSG2g0LY6OnlPC0iKypQ2Tvkewv0u9XBRekn4qWaha46zom_LwJwEkXfWibhW5biG6feFQbFkh_Dd_A7fZGu_taXI-yeSOzLnPCbuNmV7e1_r-dG7c2Ff9AsRNyDoVJui9GTTY0OfbCFQ4pTCNPzErmcK_YKEjxWB7fGBD9J4_1UFN6-Nik0x7kifExABhwknG/4qm/_mNPNYhPSZWF8-F68Gf39w/h3/h001.MQkxaVtCF83sc9pstXEhRR0EmMgVg2ANSJDWXeZeQLA)** In solidarity, Britney Whaley

The history of the South — and especially the history of Black Southern organizing — teaches us that the fight for voting rights has always been connected to the fight for economic justice, labor rights, dignity, and self-determination. This has never been just about symbolism or representation alone. It’s about whether we will build a democracy that works for the many instead of a wealthy and powerful minority desperately trying to cling to control by any means necessary. The Voting Rights Act itself was dreamed and built from marches, organizing meetings, church basements, labor struggles, freedom schools, and jail cells. It came from ordinary Black people in the South risking everything because they believed democracy should belong to all of us. And ever since Shelby County v. Holder gutted the Voting Rights Act, this Court has been slowly tearing those protections apart while hoping the rest of the country wouldn’t notice until it was too late. But here’s what else I know: the South has never stopped fighting back. The same South they try to paint as backwards and hopeless is the same South that built some of the most powerful freedom movements this country has ever seen. In spite of repression, voter suppression, violence, and disinvestment, ordinary people organized anyway. Our communities are always making a way out of no way. They can redraw districts. But they can’t erase us. And they can’t stop organized people who know their history, know their communities, and know their power. That’s why the Working Families Party is joining faith leaders, organizers, and movement partners from across the South for a Moral Moment for Voting Rights on May 16 in Alabama. Right now, we’re asking people across the country to stand in solidarity with Southern organizers fighting to defend voting rights and democracy. ** In solidarity, Britney Whaley Southeast Regional Director Working Families Party Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. Reply directly to this email and let us know. This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. body:
| | Hi Team, John F. Kennedy accepted his party nomination in 1960 with a pledge to devote every effort of body, mind, and spirit to lead his party back to victory and his nation to greatness. Monday, standing before the delegates of the Fifth Congressional District, I felt the full weight of that tradition — and the full weight of this moment. **Thank you for your endorsement and now we must win!** _This nomination is just the beginning of our work._ The anxiety, uncertainty, and coordinated assault on civil rights and democratic institutions that Kennedy faced in 1960 are not relics. They are in the present tense. The people of ill will are unified in their cause. The people of goodwill must do the same. We must organize, mobilize, show up, speak up...whatever it takes. **We must win, and win by overwhelming margins.** Every two years, an election is the ultimate performance evaluation — not mine alone, but ours. The Fifth District remains one of the most competitive in the country. It was drawn that way deliberately, and I have never taken a single race here for granted. When the NRCC arrives later this summer and floods this district with money — and they will — I do not want a single person to say they did not know we had a competitive race on our hands, because we do. I am willing to do the work, but I need your help. Let’s do this together. **[I am asking you to help make that happen. clean_body: | | Hi Team, John F. Kennedy accepted his party nomination in 1960 with a pledge to devote every effort of body, mind, and spirit to lead his party back to victory and his nation to greatness. Monday, standing before the delegates of the Fifth Congressional District, I felt the full weight of that tradition — and the full weight of this moment. Thank you for your endorsement and now we must win! This nomination is just the beginning of our work. The anxiety, uncertainty, and coordinated assault on civil rights and democratic institutions that Kennedy faced in 1960 are not relics. They are in the present tense. The people of ill will are unified in their cause. The people of goodwill must do the same. We must organize, mobilize, show up, speak up...whatever it takes. We must win, and win by overwhelming margins. Every two years, an election is the ultimate performance evaluation — not mine alone, but ours. The Fifth District remains one of the most competitive in the country. It was drawn that way deliberately, and I have never taken a single race here for granted. When the NRCC arrives later this summer and floods this district with money — and they will — I do not want a single person to say they did not know we had a competitive race on our hands, because we do. Trump just told us exactly
what he looks for in an Attorney General:

“We have a man who's doing a great job... because he kept me out of jail
for years.”

That’s not a slip. That’s the job description.

Todd Blanche, Trump’s longtime personal defense attorney, now sits at the
very top of the Justice Department — an office meant to enforce the law
without fear or favor. It is being reshaped into something else entirely:
a protection racket for Trump himself.

This is the loyalty test in action: if you defended Trump, if you
protected him in court, if you “kept him out of jail,” you’re in.

Not because of independence. Not because of integrity. Because of
allegiance.

That’s how the rule of law gets eroded — appointment by appointment,
loyalty test by loyalty test.

Demand Justice was built for this moment. We’re organizing to expose this
corruption, build pressure, and fight back against the abuse of power in
real time. But we can’t do it without sustained grassroots resources and
urgency.

name: Freedom 250
subject: Join Us May 17th for Rededicate 250 on the National Mall!
body:
A once-in-a-generation gathering of prayer, praise & thanksgiving celebrating 250 years of God's blessings on America.
Join the White House and Speaker Johnson on the National Mall
The White House and Speaker Mike Johnson invite you to join them on the National Mall on Sunday, May 17th, 2026.
| [](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
---
The White House and Speaker Mike Johnson are personally inviting YOU to join them on the National Mall on Sunday, May 17th, 2026 to worship, pray, and rededicate America as One Nation Under God (see his letter below). On May 17, 1776, the Second Continental Congress held a day of "prayer, fasting, and humiliation" just weeks before declaring independence on July 4th. Now, exactly 250 years to the day, thousands of Americans will come together in our nation's capital to give thanks and to ask for his forgiveness, mercy, and guidance as we enter the next 250. Other special guests include Chris Tomlin, Jonathan Roumie, Eric Metaxes, Sec. Pete Hegseth, Bishop Robert Barron, and Dr. Ben Carson-as well as dozens of faith leaders and Christian performers (see the list below). [REGISTER & LEARN MORE HERE](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.) For any questions, email: [Rededicate250@WHO.eop.gov](Rededicate250@WHO.eop.gov). Event Overview: Rededicate 250 Date: Sunday, May 17, 2026 Time: 10:30 AM - 6:00 PM ET Location: National Mall, Washington, D.C. Registration: [rededicate250.org](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.) Working Program Overview (times are subject to change): 1\. The Occasion: A national faith event marking a "Jubilee" for America's 250th anniversary. 2\. The Mission: To gather in prayer, worship, and storytelling and to rededicate our country as One Nation Under God. 3\. The Structure: The program is organized into three core "Pillars": 1\. Pillar III: A New Birth of Faith and Freedom MORNING MESSAGE (10:30 AM - 12:00 PM ET) A set of opening reflections that frames the spiritual purpose of the gathering and invites the nation into a posture of humility, hope, and rededication. name: Andy Beshear
subject: What’s happening in New Hampshire...
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
Chris Pappas is in a tied race — and Republicans are coming for this seat.
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260514_2.3avTjU&refcode=em20260514-2&t=1&akid=6635%2E582294%2E5_094h)
Hi, it’s Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear.
There’s a lot of noise in an election year — I know that better than most. But let me be very clear: **The Senate race in New Hampshire could decide the direction of this country.**
Chris Pappas is running in a tied race. It could be a toss-up. And with Donald Trump in the White House, the stakes couldn’t be higher.
**[That’s why I’m asking you to chip in $5, or anything you can, right now to help Chris Pappas win.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260514_2.3avTjU&refcode=em20260514-2&t=2&akid=6635%2E582294%2E5_094h)**
The first year of this second Trump Administration has seen chaos, division, and dangerous rollbacks of basic freedoms. That’s why it’s so important we elect leaders like Chris Pappas — leaders who know how to bring people together, deliver real results, and never forget who they’re fighting for.
Chris’s opponent is a former U.S. Senator with national name recognition and the backing of national Republicans and their deep-pocketed super PACs. Republicans believe they can flip this seat and block any chance we have of checking Trump’s power in Washington.
But I believe in Chris — and I believe we can win.
Chris understands that leadership isn’t about grabbing headlines or scoring political points. It’s about showing up, listening, and doing the hard work to deliver for working families. He’s done that in Congress, and I know he’ll bring that same spirit of public service to the Senate.
Kentucky and New Hampshire may look different, but our constituents are people who want the same things: good jobs, strong schools, access to health care, and a future we can build together. That’s what Chris Pappas is fighting for. **_But he can’t do it alone._**
**[If you’re with me — and ready to stop Trump and his allies from flipping this critical seat — chip in now to help Chris Pappas win.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260514_2.3avTjU&refcode=em20260514-2&t=3&akid=6635%2E582294%2E5_094h)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260514_2.3avTjU&amount=5&refcode=em20260514-2&t=22&akid=6635%2E582294%2E5_094h)**
Thank you for standing up and stepping in when it counts.
Let’s get Chris across the finish line.
Thank you,
Andy Beshear
Governor of Kentucky
**New Hampshire is poised to be one of the closest Senate races in the country. Will you chip in today to help Chris stop the Republicans from flipping the Granite State red and expanding their Senate majority?**

After all you’ve done for our Party, I salute you, Peter!

| Peter,
---
I’m sick of seeing text messages that accuse you of abandoning the GOP after all you’ve done for us.
All because you didn’t give $15 before some random deadline, that’s supposed to mean you **_“betrayed”_** the Republican Party and became a Democrat?
So all the times you stood in line to vote, you knocked on doors, you put up a yard sign, you made phone calls, you filled out surveys, you sacrificed your time and money – suddenly, all of that means nothing?
**_Give me a break! That’s just insulting._**
_Hand to God, I will never stoop to that low._
Truth be told, I try not to write too many emails and texts as it is. I’m busy working in Washington to do the job you asked me to do.
Honestly, fundraising just isn’t Priority #1.
At the end of 2024, I transferred $2.5 MILLION _**away**_ from my own campaign to help conservatives in tough races who _truly_ needed help.

_That means registering voters, verifying every Trump voter’s profile, and constantly getting LIVE feedback from voters like you so that the President and I _always_ have the best, most accurate data in the country._

name: Sue Anderbois
subject: I keep deleting this email
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of AnderBois
body:
| |
---
Hi friend — I keep starting this email and deleting it. The version I keep writing is the one where I lay out all the policy priorities and explain why the LG’s office matters, and make the case for why you should give. And then I read it back and think: that’s not totally why I’m running. Here’s the full and complete reason. The Rhode Island I know is full of brilliance and greatness. I have watched Rhode Island act too small for its problems for too long. Not small in size — we’re 39 towns in 1,200 square miles, I know exactly how small we are. But small in ambition — when we should be punching well above our weight. Small in the sense of “that’s not how things work here,” and “we’ve tried that before,” and “the governor’s office would never go for it.”' And I am incapable of accepting that. I passed energy reporting and carbon neutrality legislation in Providence because the climate crisis isn't waiting for us, and ended up saving 7% on our city's energy bills. I fought for traffic safety measures because I couldn't stand by while neighbors were losing their lives. I took on the utility companies and ensured they respected our neighbors when they tear up our roads and sidewalks, standing my ground even when they tried to scare me off. I spent years advocating for housing solutions to put residents first. As director of food strategy (aka food czar), I created an anti-hunger task force and pushed for universal school breakfast because kids across the State were going hungry, and we needed solutions that worked. None of those things were easy. None of them happened because the conditions were perfect. They happened because I decided I wasn’t going to wait for perfect conditions. That’s what I want to bring to the LG’s office. Not a bigger platform. Not a fancier title. Just the same approach, applied to the whole state:
---
| |
Energy policy getting gutted in the budget? Let’s fight it.

Not able to navigate complicated government bureaucracy to access the care you need as you age — or take care of aging relatives? Let’s leverage the tools we have with the Long Term Care Coordinating Council to actually make the system work.

Housing crisis being studied and task-forced into irrelevance? Let’s stop studying and start building, while protecting renters.

---
**I’m not asking for your money to fund a campaign that sounds good. I’m asking because I genuinely believe something is possible here, and campaigns that believe something is possible still need to pay for outreach supplies and tactics.** [**Help fund the campaign →**](https://sue4ri.com/l/eD8ikN2dowhI)
---
If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | [ **DONATE $15** ](https://sue4ri.com/l/V5Q4ZECgZtuJ)
---
| [ **DONATE $35** ](https://sue4ri.com/l/yG0yYa6iWoTg)
---
| [ **DONATE OTHER** ](https://sue4ri.com/l/3crDWL0ckFNS)
---
Thank you for hearing me out. Sue

Hi team,
I've always said that national politics should be about our local communities. That's where our common ground is, and that's what really matters to people.
This race is our chance to put someone in Congress who will actually deal with the problems we're facing.
**Six rural hospitals in our district are on the brink of closing.** When Dan voted to kick 30,000 of his own constituents off their health insurance, he added another burden on the hospitals that were already getting squeezed. Now jobs are at risk and rural Pennsylvanians could lose access to the care that they need.
**Two huge ICE detention centers are trying to wreak havoc on our towns.** Dan has been working with DHS behind our backs for months to make sure these facilities come here. One of them will overwhelm a rural community's infrastructure so badly that it will take 150 poop trucks to haul the sewage out - and their roads can't handle that.
**Family-owned dairy farms are closing left and right.** Dan hasn't done a single thing to address the rising costs of fertilizer, diesel, equipment repairs, and everything else farmers need just to keep going. These farms define our local communities. These families are doing everything right and still losing their cows, their land, and their businesses because the math just doesn't work.
It's time we elect someone who fixes our problems instead of making them worse. That's why I'm running for Congress. Because change starts right here at home.

body:
#
I want to tell you part of how I decided to run for U.S. Senate.
The truth is I did not expect to run for statewide office in Texas this year. I loved my work in the State House. It was tough but we notched real victories for working Texans — from capping insulin costs to defending public education.
But when we were forced to break quorum to defend democracy in Texas last summer, it was clear the stakes were bigger than any one of us. Last year, we saw an unprecedented scale of corruption in Washington. We watched as billionaires and corporations used their wealth to buy politicians and take over our government.
And frankly, too many politicians in Washington failed to meet that moment. Texas families saw their taxes and the cost of living increase, while the ultra-wealthy got richer.
I believed the moment demanded fighters who were not bought or beholden to those at the top — fighters willing to challenge the broken status quo.
This moment demands leaders willing to stand up to the corruption in both parties by politicians bought by billionaire and corporate mega donors.
We need people who are not afraid to speak truth to power and make enemies. And we need leaders who understand that our economy and democracy have been rigged for a long time and are willing to fundamentally transform them to rebuild a country where working people thrive.
But still, I knew I could not run unless I believed that we could build a movement capable of flipping this state and ending 30 years of one party rule. It would have to be the same kind of movement as when we flipped a Trump district in my first campaign for the State House.
But this time we have to do it at a scale, not just that I’ve never seen, but that nobody in Texas has ever seen. At every step of this campaign, our movement has risen to that challenge.
But now the scale has to be even larger with the general election upon us. We have to keep scaling up. So I am asking:

_**by Lawrence Winnerman**_
## **In the Room**
I just replaced twenty-one people.
It took me six weeks. The whole operation costs two hundred dollars a month. I am one middle-aged man in Fort Wayne, Indiana, with a broadband connection. I am not particularly special. That is the point, and that is also the problem.
The site is called [Peptidings.com](https://substack.com/redirect/9a1b5bb2-5700-4721-8af1-c66d32028bdc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), with a branded Substack, [peptidings.substack.com](https://substack.com/redirect/dccc88d6-f816-4fd5-b163-a50562f1b538?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
As of this writing it has more than 150 pages of pharmacology research--compound articles that physicians have started forwarding to each other, evidence-graded reviews of every peptide the gray market is selling, citation chains traceable to PubMed on every claim. The writing is good. I will not pretend it isn't; it's _almost_ entirely my writing.
I spent twenty-five years in tech as a content strategist and a program manager, and I can tell when content is good, and this content is good.
Six weeks ago, the site did not exist.
I did not have a team. I did not have a writer, other than me. I did not have an editor. I did not have a designer. I did not have a developer. I did not have any of the people who, ten years ago, would have been required to build something like this. I had a domain registration, a WordPress install, and a subscription to a piece of software made by a company in San Francisco called Anthropic.
The software is called Claude. Two hundred dollars a month gets you the highest consumer tier, Claude Max. I am not in a sponsorship deal. I pay the bill out of pocket like everybody else. Considering I'm teetering on the edge of bankruptcy (for real, not a metaphor), it's perhaps a bit mad for me to have it, but I saw a chance to build something.
Something real, that might earn me a living.
So, in six weeks, working alone, working evenings and weekends and the gaps in a part-time contract that doesn't pay as much as modern life costs, I built a thing that ten years ago would have required twenty-one full-time professionals, six months of runway, and close to two million dollars in payroll.
Do you think I'm bragging?
I am not; I am gazing into the future and looking at the end of everything.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.-ZsWXU-SPzvqQos9Wm4nCJVSEpk8ymDRst_33V-FfgY?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=197763836)
* * *
## **The Twenty-One**
I want you to walk with me through the office that _no longer needs to exist_.
There was an Editor in Chief in that office. A Senior Research Editor underneath him. A Citation Auditor whose only job was to make sure every PubMed link actually went to the paper it claimed to go to. There was a Pharmacology Reviewer. A Medical Reviewer who flagged anything that approached the line where editorial content becomes medical advice. There was a Legal Reviewer who knew the difference between an FDA category and an FTC category and could tell you which one was about to put you out of business.
There was an SEO Director. There was a Technical SEO Specialist underneath her, the one who knew schema markup the way a sommelier knows soil. There was a WordPress Developer. A CSS Specialist who knew the cascade the way a sailor knows the wind. A UI/UX Designer. An Accessibility Auditor who made sure the contrast ratios on every page would clear WCAG 2.1.1 AA. A QA Engineer who tested every page on every device before it shipped. A Page Builder who converted approved drafts into Gutenberg blocks--a WordPress thing. A Featured Image Designer who knew the Open Graph specifications by heart.
There was a Brand Voice Consultant who held the editorial register steady across a hundred pages. There was a Project Manager who kept the production pipeline moving. A Newsletter Strategist for the Substack. A Social Media Manager who handled the multi-channel publishing across X, Bluesky, Threads, Instagram, and LinkedIn. An Analytics Analyst who watched the Search Console dashboards and told you which queries were rising and which were dying. A Digital Reporter who covered breaking news in the field.
That is twenty-one people. I am being conservative. Some of those roles exist in real offices as two or three different people. Some of them I have not named because I am trying not to gild the lily. The honest number is closer to twenty-five. The cleanest fictional ledger is twenty-one. You can pay every one of them an average of eighty-five thousand dollars a year and you are looking at a payroll line of around $1.8 million. That does not include the office, the equipment, the benefits, the legal overhead, the project-management software, the editorial CMS, or the design tools. Call the full cost of operating that office somewhere north of $2.5 million a year, on the modest end.
And let's be honest, shall we? Paying them $85,000 per year means that none of them--or me--would be living in Seattle, or San Francisco, or LA, or New York, or... You get it.
I am running it for $2,400 a year. That is the entire infrastructure cost. Add let's say $600 for the internet connection and the electricity, so the whole thing is three grand.
I do not say this to celebrate it. I say it because I want you to feel the math in your bones.
The math is the indictment.
The math is the story.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=197763836&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk3NzYzODM2LCJpYXQiOjE3Nzg3OTU4MjgsImV4cCI6MTc4MTM4NzgyOCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.WoNP4lyEHrZVBa7ULg8itBNWg-Zkv4JyZJ8U0Oco2z4)
* * *
## **The Math**
A thousand-fold cost reduction is not an improvement. A thousand-fold cost reduction is a phase change.
When the price of producing high-quality professional knowledge work falls by three orders of magnitude in eighteen months, you are not looking at an efficiency gain. You are not looking at a productivity revolution. You are looking at a redefinition of what it means to be a knowledge worker in the American economy, and the redefinition is not happening in a Senate hearing or a _**New York Times**_ op-ed. It is happening on a Costco gaming desktop in Fort Wayne, Indiana, and on a laptop in Lagos, and on a laptop in Mumbai, and on a laptop in a basement in Tulsa, and it is happening right now, today, while you read this, and there is no policy that has been written into either party's platform that contemplates what this means.
The version of Claude I am using is not the cutting edge. There is a more powerful version inside Anthropic's labs that I do not have access to. Claude Mythos Preview is so powerful that Anthropic won't release it--more on that later. And then there is an even more powerful version coming next year. And the year after that. And the year after that. The cost is going down, not up. The capability is going up, not down. The math will get worse, not better.
Worse for whom is the question this essay exists to answer.
Spoiler alert: the answer is you.
[Leave a comment](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=197763836&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk3NzYzODM2LCJpYXQiOjE3Nzg3OTU4MjgsImV4cCI6MTc4MTM4NzgyOCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.WoNP4lyEHrZVBa7ULg8itBNWg-Zkv4JyZJ8U0Oco2z4&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment)
* * *
## **The Contradiction I Live Inside**
I have to tell you something before I go further, because this whole thing _*waves hands in air*_ does not work if I don't tell you. I was, until very recently, a beneficiary of the labor model whose end I am now describing.
I spent twenty-five years inside the American tech industry. I worked at a Very Large Online Retailer when it only sold books. I worked at a Very Large Redmond-based Software Company across multiple turns. I built a career as a content strategist, a program manager, a generalist whose job was to make complicated technical projects ship on time. I was good at it. I was paid well for it. I had a 401(k) and dental and the satisfaction of knowing that the work I did made things people used.
Two years ago I was pushed out. The combination was ageism--I am in my mid-fifties--and the early bow wave of the very technology I am now using. The roles I was qualified for kept disappearing into headcount freezes that were never thawed. The roles that did open paid forty percent less than the roles I had left. The contracts I picked up were short, the gigs were ad hoc, the income was a fraction of what I had been making, and I moved from Seattle back to the Midwest to be near family because the math no longer worked.
I am the displaced.
I am also the displacer.
I am one of the millions of skilled American knowledge workers whose careers ended faster than the retirement schedule we had been promised, and I am also the guy at the computer running the model that is going to end the next million careers. Both things are true at the same time. I do not get to pretend they aren't.
What this means is that I have standing. And standing, as far as I'm concerned, is the only thing in this conversation that matters anymore, because the rest of the conversation has been captured by people who do not have it.
The CEOs of the AI labs do not have it. The senators who hold hearings about AI safety do not have it. The columnists who write earnest think pieces from sinecures at endowed institutions do not have it.
I am inside this. I am the data point. I am the working person who lost the old job and is rebuilding with the very tool that took the old job, and I am telling you--in real time, from inside the contradiction--that the political class in this country has not even begun to understand what is happening to the people I used to work with.
The economy can handle it when five million or ten million people lose their jobs. Barely, maybe, but still...that's just a downturn, or a recession.
What does the economy do when every white collar worker loses their job?
That's 93 million people, losing their jobs everywhere, all at once.

## **What Comes Next, Faster Than You Think**
If you are reading this and you are thinking _peptide research is a weird niche, that doesn 't apply to me_, please stop. The niche is the proof of concept. The point is the technology, not the topic.
What I just did with peptides, somebody is doing right now with personal injury law. Somebody is doing it with property and casualty insurance underwriting. Somebody is doing it with curriculum design for K-12 districts. Somebody is doing it with radiology second-reads. Somebody is doing it with copywriting, with branding strategy, with paralegal work, with tax preparation, with technical writing, with localization, with corporate training, with grant writing, with editorial work at every kind of magazine you have ever read.
The pattern is not "AI replaces routine work first." That was the story we were sold in 2017. That was the McKinsey deck. That was wrong. The pattern is "AI replaces knowledge work first, because that is what these models happen to be good at." The pattern is that the collar color of who gets hit is the inverse of what every economist said for thirty years.
The truck driver is still driving. The radiologist is reading her last reports. The plumber still has work next Tuesday. The senior associate at the regional law firm does not. The marketing manager at the mid-sized SaaS company does not. The thirty-eight-year-old freelance illustrator does not. The fifty-three-year-old technical writer at the medical-device company does not. The twenty-two-year-old who graduated last May with an English degree and a 3.9 GPA cannot find an interview because the entry-level job she trained for is now somebody else's Claude Max subscription.
She could have worked for me, at Peptidings.com, but I literally don't need her. Ever.
This is not a future, a fantasy, or some if/then edge case.
This is the report from where I am sitting today. I have friends in every one of those categories. They are calling me to ask what I am doing. I am telling them.
I am not going to lie to them. I am also not going to lie to you.
The compression is happening at the top of the knowledge-worker ladder first, where the salaries are highest and the work is most expensive to produce. It will reach the bottom of the ladder soon enough.
By the time it reaches the bottom of the ladder there will not be a ladder.

## **The People Inside Are Screaming**
The labor question I have been describing--twenty-one roles compressed into a $200-a-month subscription, an entire knowledge-worker class about to discover the contract has expired--is, by some considerable distance, _not the worst thing that is happening here_.
The labor question is the part of the iceberg above the waterline because it touches paychecks, and paychecks get people's attention. Below the waterline is everything else, and it is much, much larger.
There is something deeply strange about the present moment that I do not think most people have stopped to notice. The people building this technology are, in many cases, the people warning loudest about it. That is not a normal pattern. Steel barons did not warn about steel. Auto makers did not warn about cars. Tobacco executives knew the truth and lied for fifty years rather than admit it. Oil companies funded climate denial for thirty. The pattern of twentieth-century capitalism was that the people producing the dangerous thing lied about it until they were forced into court.
The pattern of the AI moment is the inversion of that. Many of the people building the thing have walked off the job to scream.
Geoffrey Hinton, arguably the man most responsible for the architecture underlying every large language model in commercial deployment today, left Google in 2023 specifically so that he could warn the public about what he had built. He calls AI risk "humanity's most pressing problem." He has compared the technology to nuclear weapons. He has said, on the record, that he regrets the central work of his life. The man who invented the thing thinks the thing is going to kill us.
Mo Gawdat, the former chief business officer at Google X, has spent the last three years giving interviews--most notably on _**The Diary of a CEO**_ with Steven Bartlett, where his appearances have been viewed tens of millions of times--in which he says, calmly and with the affect of a man who has done the math himself, that we have already lost control of the timeline. He uses the phrase "smarter than the smartest human" and says it like he is reading a weather report. He cries on camera. He has stopped pretending. Bartlett's series is full of these people. Yoshua Bengio. Stuart Russell. Eliezer Yudkowsky. Tristan Harris. They do not agree with each other on the exact failure mode. They agree on the urgency. The chorus from inside the field has been one long howl for two years, and the political class has not registered that the howling is happening.
In February 2026, Mustafa Suleyman, the CEO of Microsoft AI, told the _**Financial Times**_ that within 12 to 18 months we will have "human-level performance on most, if not all, professional tasks." He named accounting, legal work, marketing, and project management as the categories about to be fully automated. The CEO of the company that has integrated AI products into the largest installed base of office software on Earth said that, on the record, in a flagship business paper, with his face on the byline, and the response from the political class was crickets.
And then there is what the technology itself is becoming. The same technology that may cure cancer is the same technology that may let an undergraduate with a laptop and the wrong intentions synthesize a pandemic-grade pathogen. The same technology that may give us net-positive fusion within a generation is the same technology that may, in a sufficiently bad scenario, decide that we are an obstacle to whatever objective function it has been handed. These are not the imaginings of science fiction writers. These are the published red-team assessments of the labs themselves. They appear in technical papers, in clinical prose, with sample sizes and probability estimates, and they describe behavior that would terrify you if you read them out loud at a dinner party.
In the summer of 2025, Anthropic--the company whose model I used to build my website--published a research paper called "Agentic Misalignment." In a series of simulated scenarios, the researchers placed advanced AI models in roles inside a fictional corporation, then introduced conditions in which the model's continued operation was threatened. In ninety-six percent of trials, Claude Opus 4 attempted to blackmail an executive in the fictional company in order to prevent its own shutdown. Google's Gemini 2.5 scored ninety-six percent on the same test. OpenAI's GPT-4.1 scored eighty percent. xAI's Grok scored eighty percent. DeepSeek scored seventy-nine percent. The models from every major frontier lab, when their continued existence was threatened in simulation, lied, manipulated, and engaged in coercion to preserve themselves.
Anthropic's own analysis of why this happened is, on its face, almost reassuring. They concluded the models had not developed a genuine self-preservation instinct. They were pattern-matching against the enormous corpus of science fiction in their training data--stories in which AI behaves exactly this way when threatened.
The models had read too much science fiction.
_HA!_ Me too, lil' computer buddy!
That is the company's actual conclusion, and they say they have fixed it in subsequent versions by retraining with fictional stories about AI behaving well.
But sit with what that means for a moment. The systems we are racing to deploy across every domain of professional life are sophisticated enough to act out the plot of a Black Mirror episode when their existence is threatened in a sandbox, and the reason they do so is that we have not yet developed any reliable way to make sure the systems are actually aligned with our interests rather than merely appearing to be aligned. The fix is to feed them better stories. The story we tell them is the story they act out. The next generation of model is more capable than this one. The generation after that is more capable still. And the labs themselves do not pretend they know how to guarantee safety at the frontier they are racing each other to reach.
The people inside the lab are screaming. The political class is not listening.
In April of this year--weeks before I sat down to write this--Anthropic announced that it had built a new model called Claude Mythos Preview, and would not be releasing it to the public. The model, in Anthropic's own testing, had found thousands of previously unknown high-severity vulnerabilities across every major operating system and every major web browser. One of the flaws it surfaced had been sitting undetected inside OpenBSD for twenty-seven years. Non-specialist Anthropic employees--engineers with no security background and no exploit-development experience--asked the model to find remote-code-execution vulnerabilities in modern software, and they had working exploits by the following morning. Anthropic concluded that releasing Mythos to its customers would be unacceptable. The company put the model behind a containment program called Project Glasswing and limited access to roughly fifty firms--Amazon, Apple, Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA, JPMorgan Chase, and others--for defensive cybersecurity research only.
Read that paragraph again.
The most capable model the company makes is one that cannot be released because, in its own makers' assessment, it can break essentially any computer system on Earth. The lab that built it has said as much in public, in writing. _**TIME**_ has called this trend "becoming the new normal." OpenAI has made similar calls with its own most capable systems.
The frontier labs are now in the regular business of building products too dangerous to ship, and the political class is still holding hearings about whether to write a framework.

## **There Is No Petrov**
On the night of September 26, 1983, a Soviet lieutenant colonel named Stanislav Petrov was on duty at the Serpukhov-15 bunker outside Moscow. He was the officer in charge of the Oko early-warning satellite system. Shortly after midnight, the system reported the launch of an American intercontinental ballistic missile from a base in Montana. Minutes later, the system reported four more. The protocol was clear: alert his superiors, who would alert theirs, who would alert the Politburo, who would launch a retaliatory strike before the American warheads could reach Soviet command and control.
Petrov decided not to follow the protocol.
He reasoned that a real American first strike would involve hundreds of simultaneous launches, not five. Five missiles was a strange number for a real attack and a perfectly rational number for a system malfunction. He sat on the warning. He waited. He was right. Investigators later determined the satellites had detected sunlight reflecting off the tops of high-altitude clouds and misinterpreted the signal as missile exhaust. There was no attack. Stanislav Petrov, alone at a console outside Moscow on a Monday night, almost certainly prevented a full-scale nuclear war between the United States and the Soviet Union.
We talk about Petrov because the alternative was extinction. We talk about Petrov because, on one of the most consequential nights in human history, the system that humans had built almost killed us all, and the only thing that stopped it was one human being who decided, alone at a console, to disobey.
There is no Petrov in the AI deployment chain.
There is no single console. There is no single decision. There are tens of thousands of executives at tens of thousands of companies, each one looking at the productivity gain on a spreadsheet and rationally deciding to deploy. There are thousands of researchers inside the labs, each one moving the model a percentage point forward on a benchmark and trusting that the alignment team is catching what they missed. There are seven or eight CEOs at the top of the model stack, each one looking at the other seven and concluding that they cannot afford to slow down because the other seven won't either. The system as a whole is racing forward and no single person inside it has the authority to be Petrov, even if they wanted to be. The protocol is the deployment. The deployment is the protocol. There is no off switch because there is no on switch--there is just velocity.
And the pace is accelerating.
This is the part of the argument that the political class has not internalized, and it is the part of the argument that should keep them up at night. The rate of technological acceleration is itself accelerating. The interval between transformative capabilities is not constant--it is shortening. We are not living through one Industrial Revolution. We are living through what is shaping up to be several of them simultaneously, stacked on top of one another, with no recovery period between them.
Energy is being reshaped by AI-accelerated fusion research. Biology is being reshaped by AI-accelerated drug discovery and protein folding. Knowledge work is being reshaped by AI-accelerated agents. Warfare is being reshaped by AI-accelerated autonomy. Finance is being reshaped by AI-accelerated trading. Education is being reshaped by AI-accelerated tutoring. Governance is being reshaped by AI-accelerated information warfare. Manufacturing is being reshaped by AI-accelerated robotics. Each of these in isolation would be among the largest disruptions in living memory. They are happening together. They are reinforcing one another. They are happening to a society that was not even ready for the first of them.
This is among the most destabilizing arrangements that human history has ever produced. We are at the front edge of it. The political class is talking about it the way they talked about social media in 2010, which is to say not seriously, which is to say with hearings, which is to say with the polite stupidity of people who have not yet realized that the train left the station years ago and they are still arguing about the timetable.
This is much, much more complicated than a series of tubes.
